title.zh: 卷六十五 吳書二十 王樓賀韋華傳
title.en: Volume 65: Book of Wu 20 - Biographies of Wang, Lou, He, Wei, and Hua
title.raw: 卷六十五 吳書二十 王樓賀韋華傳 Volume 65: Book of Wu 20 - Biographies of Wang, Lou, He, Wei, and Hua

sentences.zh: 王蕃字永元，廬江人也。

translations.literal: Wang Fan, courtesy name Yongyuan, was a man of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan, courtesy name Yongyuan, came from Lujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 博覽多聞，兼通術藝。

translations.literal: He read widely and heard much, and was also versed in technical arts.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely read and well informed, and equally at home with astronomy, mathematics, and the technical arts.

sentences.zh: 始為尚書郎，去官。

translations.literal: At first he was gentleman of the masters of writing, then left office.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a gentleman clerk in the secretariat, then resigned his post.

sentences.zh: 孫休即位，與賀邵、薛瑩、虞汜俱為散騎中常侍，皆加駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: When Sun Xiu ascended the throne, together with He Shao, Xue Ying, and Yu Si he became all attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, and to each was added chief commandant of carriage escort.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Xiu took the throne, Wang Fan, He Shao, Xue Ying, and Yu Si were all named attendants at ease and regular palace attendants, each with the additional title chief commandant of carriage escort.

sentences.zh: 時論清之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion deemed them pure.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion ranked them among the court's clearest spirits.

sentences.zh: 遣使至蜀，蜀人稱焉，還為夏口監軍。

translations.literal: He was sent as envoy to Shu; the people of Shu praised him, and on return he became supervisor of the army at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Sent on embassy to Shu, he won high praise there; on his return he was named supervisor of the army at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 孫皓初。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Sun Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Sun Hao's reign.

sentences.zh: 復入為常侍，與萬彧同官。

translations.literal: Again he entered as regular attendant, holding the same office as Wan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as regular attendant, serving alongside Wan Yu.

sentences.zh: 彧與皓有舊，俗士挾侵，謂蕃自輕。

translations.literal: Yu had old ties with Hao; vulgar gentlemen, bearing encroachment, said Fan belittled himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Yu was an old friend of the emperor, and shallow courtiers, nursing slights, whispered that Wang Fan looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 又中書丞陳聲，皓之嬖臣，數譖毀蕃。

translations.literal: Moreover secretariat aide Chen Sheng was Hao's favored minister and repeatedly slandered and ruined Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Sheng, aide in the secretariat and Sun Hao's favorite, kept whispering slander against Wang Fan.

sentences.zh: 蕃體氣高亮，不能承顏順指；

translations.literal: Fan's bearing and spirit were lofty and bright; he could not read the ruler's mood and comply with hints;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan carried himself with stiff dignity and would not truckle or read every twitch of the imperial brow;

sentences.zh: 時或迕意，積以見責。

translations.literal: At times he went against intent, and by accumulation came to be blamed.
translations.idiomatic: He sometimes crossed the emperor, and rebuke piled up against him.

sentences.zh: 甘露二年，丁忠使晉還，皓大會群臣，蕃沉醉頓伏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Ganlu, Ding Zhong returned from mission to Jin; Hao held a great assembly of the assembled ministers, and Fan was dead drunk and collapsed prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Ganlu (266), when Ding Zhong returned from his mission to Jin, Sun Hao feasted the whole court; Wang Fan drank himself insensible and slumped forward.

sentences.zh: 皓疑而不悅，舉蕃出外。

translations.literal: Hao suspected and was not pleased; he had Fan lifted and taken outside.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao took offense at his condition and had him carried from the hall.

sentences.zh: 頃之請還，酒亦不解。

translations.literal: Shortly he requested to return, yet the wine also did not clear.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to come back in, still far from sober.

sentences.zh: 蕃性有威嚴，行止自若，皓大怒，呵左右於殿下斬之。

translations.literal: Fan by nature had awe-inspiring dignity; in deportment he was self-possessed as before; Hao was greatly angry and shouted to those at his sides to behead him below the hall steps.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan bore himself with unbending dignity; Sun Hao flew into a rage and ordered his guards to cut him down below the steps.

sentences.zh: 衛將軍滕牧、征西將軍留平請，不能得。

translations.literal: General of the guards Teng Mu and general who campaigns west Liu Ping pleaded, but could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: General Teng Mu and General Liu Ping begged for his life, but Sun Hao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：皓用巫史之言，谓建业宫不利，乃西巡武昌，仍有迁都之意，恐群臣不从，乃大请会，赐将吏。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Hao followed the words of shamans and clerks, saying the Jianye palace was inauspicious; thereupon he toured west to Wuchang, still having the intent to move the capital, and fearing the assembled ministers would not follow, he greatly invited a meeting and bestowed gifts on generals and clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan relates that Sun Hao, heeding sorcerers who called the Jianye palace ill-omened, moved west to Wuchang while planning a full change of capital; fearing opposition, he summoned a grand banquet for officers and showered them with gifts.

sentences.zh: 问蕃“射不主皮，为力不同科，其义云何”？

translations.literal: He asked Fan: "Archery does not take mastery of the hide as its main point, for strength has different grades—what is the meaning of this?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked Wang Fan what the Analects meant by "In archery, piercing the hide is not the point; strength differs by rank."

sentences.zh: 蕃思惟未答，即於殿上斩蕃。

translations.literal: Fan thought and did not answer; immediately on the hall steps he beheaded Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wang Fan could answer, Sun Hao had him executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 出登来山，使亲近将

translations.literal: He went out and ascended Mount Lai, ordering those intimate to lead
translations.idiomatic: He went out to Mount Lai and ordered his attendants to take

translations.literal: (leap / toss)
translations.idiomatic: —toss—

sentences.zh: 蕃首，作虎跳狼争咋齧之，头皆碎坏，欲以示威，使众不敢犯也。

translations.literal: Fan's head—making tigers leap and wolves contend to bite and gnaw it—the skull was smashed to pieces, desiring thereby to display awe and make the multitude not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: They took Wang Fan's head and staged tiger leaps and wolf bites until the skull was pulp, hoping to cow the assembly into silence.

sentences.zh: 此与本传不同。

translations.literal: This differs from the main biography.
translations.idiomatic: This version disagrees with the main biography.

sentences.zh: 吴录曰：皓每於会，因酒酣，辄令侍臣嘲谑公卿，以为笑乐。

translations.literal: The Wu lu states: Whenever Hao was at a gathering, because wine ran high, he always ordered attendant ministers to jeer and mock dukes and ministers, taking it as laughter and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu lu notes that at feasts, once the wine flowed, Sun Hao habitually made his attendants ridicule the high ministers for sport.

sentences.zh: 万彧既为左丞相，蕃嘲彧曰：“鱼潜於渊，出水煦沫。

translations.literal: When Wan Yu had become left chancellor, Fan mocked Yu, saying: "Fish hide in the deep; coming out of the water they warm the foam with their breath.
translations.idiomatic: After Wan Yu became left chancellor, Wang Fan needled him: "Fish belong in the deep;

sentences.zh: 何则？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why is that?

sentences.zh: 物有本性，不可横处非分也。

translations.literal: Things have their proper nature; one cannot recklessly dwell beyond one's allotment.
translations.idiomatic: Every creature has its proper place—you cannot usurp a station that is not yours.

sentences.zh: 彧出自谿谷，羊质虎皮，虚受光赫之宠，跨越三九之位，犬马犹能识养，将何以报厚施乎！

translations.literal: Yu came from ravine and valley—sheep's substance, tiger's skin—empty receiving dazzling favor, leaping across the three-nine ranks; dogs and horses still know how to repay nurture—how will you repay thick bounty!
translations.idiomatic: You crawled from a backwater yet wear a tiger's pelt: you soak up glory and vault over ranks you never earned. Even dogs and horses know gratitude—how will you repay such bounty?

sentences.zh: ”彧曰：“唐虞之朝无谬举之才，造父之门无驽蹇之质，蕃上诬明选，下讪桢幹，何伤於日月，適多见其不知量耳。

translations.literal: " Yu said: "In the court of Tang and Yu there were no wrongly promoted talents; at Zaofu's gate there were no lame-nag natures—Fan above slanders clear selection, below mocks the state's pillars—what harm to sun and moon? It only much shows his not knowing measure.
translations.idiomatic: "Wan Yu retorted: "Under Yao and Shun no fool was promoted; at Zaofu's stable no cripple nags were kept. Wang Fan slanders the civil service above and mocks the state's timber below—he does not scratch the sun and moon; he only shows how little he knows his own measure.

sentences.zh: ”臣松之按本传云丁忠使晋还，皓为大会，於会中杀蕃，检忠从北还在此年之春，彧时尚未为丞相，至秋乃为相耳。

translations.literal: " Your servant Songzhi notes the main biography says Ding Zhong returned from Jin and Hao held a great assembly, killing Fan in the assembly; examining Zhong's return from the north, it was in the spring of this year—Yu at that time was not yet chancellor; only in autumn did he become chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: "Pei Songzhi observes that the main text places Wang Fan's death at Ding Zhong's return feast in the spring of that year, when Wan Yu was not yet chancellor—he became chancellor only in autumn.

sentences.zh: 吴录所言为乖互不同。〉

translations.literal: The words of the Wu lu are contradictory and do not agree."
translations.idiomatic: The Wu lu account therefore conflicts with the standard biography."

sentences.zh: 丞相陸凱上疏曰："常侍王蕃黃中通理，知天知物，處朝忠蹇，斯社稷之重鎮，大吳之龍逢也。

translations.literal: Chancellor Lu Kai submitted a memorial saying: "Regular attendant Wang Fan is yellow within and comprehends principle; he knows Heaven and knows things; in court he is loyal and outspoken—he is the heavy bulwark of the altars of soil and grain, the Long Pang of great Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kai memorialized: "Wang Fan is the inner integrity and clear judgment of the court—Wu's pillar, your Long Pang.

sentences.zh: 昔事景皇，納言左右，景皇欽嘉，歎為異倫。

translations.literal: In former times he served Emperor Jing, speaking out at the ruler's side; Emperor Jing admired and praised him, sighing that he was of a different class.
translations.idiomatic: He served Emperor Jing as a candid advisor and won that emperor's open admiration.

sentences.zh: 而陛下忿其苦辭，惡其直對，梟之殿堂，屍骸暴棄，邦內傷心，有識悲悼。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty resented his bitter words, hated his straight replies, displayed him in the hall, and his corpse was cast aside exposed—within the state hearts are wounded, those with understanding mourn in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you resented his blunt speech, executed him in open court, and left his body unburied—the whole court grieves, every thoughtful man mourns.

sentences.zh: "其痛蕃如此。

translations.literal: " Thus he grieved for Fan to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Lu Kai's grief for Wang Fan."

sentences.zh: 蕃死時年三十九，皓徙蕃家屬廣州。

translations.literal: When Fan died he was thirty-nine years old; Hao moved Fan's family dependants to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan died at thirty-nine; Sun Hao banished his kin to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二弟著、延皆作佳器，郭馬起事，不為馬用，見害。

translations.literal: His two younger brothers Zhu and Yan were both fine vessels; when Guo Ma raised an affair, they would not serve Ma and were killed.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Wang Zhu and Wang Yan were both promising men; when Guo Ma rose in revolt they refused to serve him and were put to death.

sentences.zh: 樓玄字承先，沛郡蘄人也。

translations.literal: Lou Xuan, courtesy name Chengxian, was a man of Qi in Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Xuan, courtesy name Chengxian, came from Qi in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 孫休時為監農御史。

translations.literal: In Sun Xiu's time he was censor who supervises agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Xiu he served as censor of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 孫皓即位，與王蕃、郭逴、萬彧俱為散騎中常侍，出為會稽太守，入為大司農。

translations.literal: When Sun Hao ascended the throne, together with Wang Fan, Guo Chuo, and Wan Yu he became all attendant at ease and regular palace attendant; he went out as grand administrator of Kuaiji and entered as grand minister of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao took the throne, Lou Xuan joined Wang Fan, Guo Chuo, and Wan Yu as attendants at ease and regular palace attendants, then served as grand administrator of Kuaiji and grand minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 舊禁中主者自用親近人作之，彧陳親密近職宜用好人，皓因敕有司，求忠清之士，以應其選，遂用玄為宮下鎮禁中候，主殿中事，玄從九卿持刀侍衛，正身率眾，奉法而行，應對切直，數迕皓意，漸見責怒。

translations.literal: By old practice those in charge within the forbidden precincts always used intimate men for the post; Yu presented that intimate near offices ought to employ good men; Hao thereupon ordered the responsible offices to seek loyal and pure gentlemen to meet that selection, and so used Xuan as palace-base colonel who garrisons the forbidden interior, in charge of hall affairs—Xuan, ranking with the nine ministers, bore the blade as bodyguard, corrected his person and led the host, acted by the law, answered cuttingly and straight, repeatedly went against Hao's intent, and gradually met blame and anger.
translations.idiomatic: Palace posts had always gone to favorites; Wan Yu urged that inner offices need honest men. Sun Hao then picked Lou Xuan as colonel of the palace guard, equal to the nine ministers, carrying the imperial blade—Lou enforced the law, spoke plainly, crossed the emperor often, and drew mounting wrath.

sentences.zh: 後人誣白玄與賀邵相逢，駐共耳語大笑，謗訕政事，遂被詔詰責，送付廣州。

translations.literal: Afterward someone falsely reported that Xuan, meeting He Shao, halted and together whispered in the ear and laughed greatly, slandering and mocking government affairs; thereupon he received an edict of interrogation and blame and was sent off to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later a informer claimed he had stopped in the road with He Shao, whispered and laughed, and mocked policy; an edict condemned him and he was banished to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 東觀令華核上疏曰：

translations.literal: Director of the Eastern Institute Hua He submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Hua He, director of the Eastern Institute, memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣竊以治國之體，其猶治家。

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that the body of governing a state is like governing a family.
translations.idiomatic: Governing a state, in my humble view, is like running a household.

sentences.zh: 主田野者，皆宜良信。

translations.literal: Those who oversee field and wild ought all to be good and trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Overseers of the countryside must be honest and reliable.

sentences.zh: 又宜得一人總其條目，為作維綱，眾事乃理。

translations.literal: Moreover one ought to obtain one man to gather the threads and items, to make for them the main rope—then the multitude of affairs are ordered.
translations.idiomatic: You also need one man to hold the threads and set the net in order.

sentences.zh: 《論語》曰：『無為而治者其舜也與!恭己正南面而己。

translations.literal: The Analects says: "He who rules without action—may it not be Shun? Reverently correcting himself and facing south—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says of Shun that he "ruled without acting"—only sat south in correct dignity.

sentences.zh: 』言所任得其人，放優遊而自逸也。

translations.literal: ' It means those employed were the right men, so he could let events drift in ease and rest himself.
translations.idiomatic: That means the right men held office, so the ruler could rest easy.

sentences.zh: 今海內未定，天下多事，事無大小，皆當關聞，動經御坐，勞損聖慮。

translations.literal: Now within the seas is not settled, All-under-Heaven has many affairs; affairs great and small all ought to be reported and heard, movements always passing the imperial seat, wearing and injuring the sage's care.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still unsettled; every matter, great or small, crosses your desk and drains your spirit.

sentences.zh: 陛下既垂意博古，綜極藝文，加勤心好道，隨節致氣，宜得閑靜以展神思，呼翕清淳，與天同極。

translations.literal: Your Majesty already bends mind to broadly studying antiquity, exhausts the utmost in arts and letters, moreover diligently inclines the heart to the Way, following the seasons to harmonize qi—you ought to obtain leisure and quiet to unfold divine thought, breathing in pure simplicity, sharing the pole with Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: You study the classics, pursue the arts, and cultivate qi—you need quiet space for reflection and breath of purity to match Heaven.

sentences.zh: 臣夙夜思惟，諸吏之中，任干之事，足委丈者，無勝於樓玄。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks day and night: among the various clerks, for affairs of responsibility and management sufficient to entrust to a mature man, none surpasses Lou Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Among all officials none matches Lou Xuan for steady hands on heavy work.

sentences.zh: 玄清忠奉公，冠冕當世，眾服其操，無與爭先。

translations.literal: Xuan is pure, loyal, and serves the public; he caps the age— the multitude admire his conduct, none contends to go before him.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Xuan is incorrupt, loyal, and devoted—the court admires his integrity above all.

sentences.zh: 失清者則心平而意直，忠者惟正道而履之，如玄之性，終始可保，乞陛下赦玄前愆，使得自新，擢之宰司，責其後效。

translations.literal: He who loses purity then has a level heart and straight intent; he who is loyal treads only the correct path—as with Xuan's nature, from first to last it can be trusted; your servant prays Your Majesty will pardon Xuan's former faults, allow him to renew himself, raise him to the ministry, and charge his later effect.
translations.idiomatic: Purity steadies the mind; loyalty walks the straight road—Lou Xuan will not waver. Pardon his past errors, restore him to high office, and demand results.

sentences.zh: 使為官擇人，隨才授任，則舜之恭己，近亦可得。

translations.literal: If for office one selects men and according to talent confers appointment, then Shun's reverent self-correction can nearly be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint the worthy to fit posts and you may approach Shun's ease of rule.

sentences.zh: 皓話玄名聲，復徙玄及子據，付交阯將張奕，使以戰自效，陰別敕奕令殺之。

translations.literal: Hao took account of Xuan's reputation, again transferred Xuan and his son Ju, handed them to Jiao general Zhang Yi, ordered them to prove themselves in battle, and secretly issued a separate edict to Yi ordering him to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao, nursing a grudge against Lou Xuan's name, sent him and his son Lou Ju to General Zhang Yi in Jiao with orders to earn merit in war, while secretly instructing Zhang Yi to murder them.

sentences.zh: 據到交阯，病死。

translations.literal: When Ju reached Jiaozhi, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Ju died of illness on reaching Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 玄一身隨亦討賊，持刀步涉，見亦輒拜，亦未忍殺。

translations.literal: Xuan alone followed Yi in campaigning against bandits, carrying a blade and wading on foot; when he saw Yi he always bowed, and Yi could not bear to kill.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Xuan alone followed Zhang Yi against rebels, sword in hand, wading on foot; whenever he met Zhang Yi he bowed deeply, and Zhang could not bring himself to strike.

sentences.zh: 會亦暴卒，玄殯斂亦，於器中見敕書，還便自殺。

translations.literal: When Yi also suddenly died, Xuan encoffined Yi; in the coffin gear he saw the secret edict, and on return then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yi died suddenly, Lou Xuan prepared his body for burial and found the secret order in the baggage; he returned and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 〈江表傳曰：皓遣将张奕追赐玄鸩，奕以玄贤者，不忍即宣诏致药，玄阴知之，谓奕曰：「当早告玄，玄何惜邪？

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Hao sent general Zhang Yi to pursue and bestow poison on Xuan; Yi, because Xuan was a worthy man, could not bear immediately to proclaim the edict and deliver the drug; Xuan secretly knew it and said to Yi: "You ought early to tell Xuan—what would Xuan grudge?
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan says Sun Hao sent Zhang Yi after Lou Xuan with poison; Zhang, honoring Lou as a worthy, hesitated to announce the edict; Lou guessed the truth and told him, "Tell me plainly—I do not cling to life.

sentences.zh: 」即服药死。

translations.literal: " Immediately he took the drug and died.
translations.idiomatic: He drank the poison at once.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以玄之清高，必不以安危易操，无缘骤拜张奕，以亏其节。

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers that with Xuan's purity and elevation he surely would not for safety or peril alter his integrity, and had no reason suddenly to bow to Zhang Yi and impair his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi doubts that so principled a man would suddenly bow repeatedly to Zhang Yi and stain his honor.

sentences.zh: 且祸机既发，岂百拜所免？

translations.literal: Moreover once the trap of disaster had sprung, how could a hundred bows avoid it?
translations.idiomatic: Nor would a hundred bows avert a plot already sprung.

sentences.zh: 江表传所言，於理为长。〉

translations.literal: What the Jiangbiao zhuan says is longer in accord with principle."
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan version is the more plausible."

sentences.zh: 賀邵字興伯，會稽山陰人也，

translations.literal: He Shao, courtesy name Xingbo, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji,
translations.idiomatic: He Shao, courtesy name Xingbo, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：邵，贺齐之孙，景之子。〉

translations.literal: The Book of Wu states: Shao was grandson of He Qi, son of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu identifies him as He Qi's grandson and He Jing's son.

sentences.zh: 孫休即位，從中郎為散騎中常侍，出為吳郡太守。

translations.literal: When Sun Xiu ascended the throne, he went from gentleman of the palace to attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, and went out as grand administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Xiu took the throne he rose from gentleman of the palace to attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, then became grand administrator of Wu.

sentences.zh: 孫皓時，入為左典軍，遷中書令，領太子太傅。

translations.literal: In Sun Hao's time he entered as left master of ceremonies, was transferred to director of the secretariat, and concurrently held grand tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Hao he became left master of ceremonies, then director of the secretariat, while serving as grand tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 皓兇暴驕矜，政事日弊。

translations.literal: Hao was cruel, violent, and arrogant; day by day government affairs decayed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao grew cruel, arrogant, and daily more corrupt.

sentences.zh: 邵上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Shao submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He Shao therefore presented a memorial:

sentences.zh: 古之聖王，所以潛處重闈之內而知萬里之情，垂拱衽席之上，明照八極之際者，任賢之功也。

translations.literal: The sage kings of old, the reason they could dwell deep within layered inner chambers yet know conditions ten thousand li away, drape their sleeves on the cushion while all within the eight extremities was brightly illumined, was the work of employing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sage kings knew the realm from the inner palace because they employed worthy men.

sentences.zh: 陛下以至德淑姿，統承皇業，宜率身履道，恭奉神器，旌賢表善，以康庶政。

translations.literal: Your Majesty with utmost virtue and fine bearing inherits and receives the imperial enterprise; you ought to take the body to tread the Way, reverently uphold the sacred regalia, raise banners for the worthy and display the good, thereby bringing the multitude of tasks to peace.
translations.idiomatic: You should walk the Way, honor the throne, lift up the worthy, and set the government aright.

sentences.zh: 自頃年以來，朝列紛錯，真偽相貿，上下空任，文武曠位，外無山嶽之鎮，內無拾遺之臣。

translations.literal: From recent years onward, the court array has been tangled, true and false trade places, above and below are empty in appointment, civil and martial posts stand vacant, without mountain bulwarks on the outside, without remonstrance ministers within.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the court has been a tangle of true and false talent, offices stand empty inside and out, and neither civil nor military posts are reliably filled.

sentences.zh: 佞諛之徒拊冀天飛，干弄朝威，盜竊榮利，而忠良排墜，信臣被害。

translations.literal: Flattering sycophants flap their wings hoping to fly to Heaven, meddle with and play with court majesty, steal glory and profit, while the loyal and good are thrust aside and ruined, and trusted ministers are harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Sycophants twist imperial power while good men are cast aside and loyal officers ruined.

sentences.zh: 是以正士摧方，而庸臣苟媚，先意承旨，各希時趣。

translations.literal: Therefore straight gentlemen break their squareness, while mediocre ministers crudely flatter, anticipating intent and carrying out orders, each hoping for the moment's fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Upright men blunt their edges while mediocrities anticipate every whim.

sentences.zh: 人執反理之評，士吐詭道之論，遂使清流變濁，忠臣結舌。

translations.literal: Men hold assessments that invert principle, gentlemen give speeches of devious doctrine—thereupon clear streams turn muddy and loyal ministers seal their lips.
translations.idiomatic: Men mouth inverted judgments and clever heresies until clear streams run foul and loyal tongues fall silent.

sentences.zh: 陛下處九天之上，隱百重之室，言出風靡，令行景從，親洽寵媚之臣，日聞順意之辭，將謂此輩實賢，而天下已平也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty dwells above the nine heavens, hidden in chambers of a hundred layers; words issue like wind-blown grass, orders go like shadow following form; you draw near daily to favored flattering ministers and hear only compliant phrases—you will suppose these men are truly worthy and All-under-Heaven is already at peace.
translations.idiomatic: You sit aloft in a hundredfold palace; your word runs like wind, your command like shadow; you hear only flatterers and will think the realm already at peace.

sentences.zh: 臣心所不安，敢不以聞。

translations.literal: What your servant's heart cannot rest at ease with, he dares not fail to report.
translations.idiomatic: What troubles my heart I dare not withhold.

sentences.zh: 臣聞興國之君樂聞其過，荒亂之主樂聞其譽。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the lord who raises a state delights to hear his faults, while the lord of wasteland and chaos delights to hear his praise.
translations.idiomatic: A rising king loves to hear his faults; a doomed king loves praise.

sentences.zh: 聞其過者過日消而福臻，聞其譽者譽日損而禍至。

translations.literal: He who hears his faults—faults daily diminish and blessing arrives; he who hears his praise—praise daily shrinks and disaster comes.
translations.idiomatic: Faults heard shrink and fortune grows; praise heard swells and calamity nears.

sentences.zh: 是以古之人君，捐讓以進賢，虛己以求過，譬天位於乘□，以虎尾為警戒。

translations.literal: Therefore the lords of old yielded place to advance the worthy, emptied themselves to seek faults, likened the heavenly seat to riding a rotten log, and took the tiger's tail as warning.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients yielded to bring forward talent and took the throne as riding rotten wood beside a tiger's tail.

sentences.zh: 至於陛下，嚴刑法以禁直辭，黜善士以逆諫臣，眩耀毀譽之實，沉淪近習之言。

translations.literal: As for Your Majesty, you use harsh punishments to forbid straight speech, dismiss good gentlemen to reject remonstrating ministers, dazzle yourself with the reality of slander and praise, and sink in the words of those near at hand.
translations.idiomatic: You silence candor with cruel law, exile good men who remonstrate, chase gossip, and drown in favorites' whispers.

sentences.zh: 昔高宗思佐，夢寐得賢，而陛下求之如忘，忽之如遺。

translations.literal: In olden times Gaozong thought on helpers and in dream and sleep obtained the worthy; Your Majesty seeks them as if forgotten, neglects them as if cast away.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong dreamed his ministers; you forget yours and toss them aside.

sentences.zh: 故常侍王蕃忠恪在公，才任輔弼，以醉酒之間加之大戮。

translations.literal: Therefore regular attendant Wang Fan was loyal and careful in public service, his talent fit to assist and guide—over drunkenness in a feast you added the great execution.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan was fit to be your pillar—you slew him for a drunken slip.

sentences.zh: 近鴻臚葛奚，先帝舊臣，偶有逆迕，昏醉之言耳，三爵之後，禮所不諱，陛下猥發雷霆，謂之輕慢，飲之醇酒，中毒隕命。

translations.literal: Recently grand herald Ge Xi, an old minister of the late emperor, once by chance was contrary and disobedient—it was words of muddled drunkenness; after three goblets, what rites do not excuse—Your Majesty rashly loosed thunder, calling it slighting and irreverent, made him drink strong wine, and he was poisoned and lost his life.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Xi, an elder statesman, misspoke while drunk—rites forgive what follows three cups—yet you called it lese-majesty, forced strong wine on him, and he died of poison.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，海內悼心，朝臣失圖，仕者以退為幸，居者以出為福，誠非所以保光洪緒，臣隆道化也。

translations.literal: From this time within the seas mourn in heart, court ministers lose their bearings; those in office take retirement as fortune, those at home take going out as blessing—this is truly not the means to preserve the bright great line and extend the transforming Way.
translations.idiomatic: Officials now count leaving office as luck and staying home as blessing—no way to preserve the dynasty or spread moral rule.

sentences.zh: 又何定本趨走小人，僕隸之下，身無錙銖之行，能無鷹犬之用，而陛下愛其佞媚，假其威柄，使定恃寵放恣，自擅威福，口正國議，手弄天機，上虧日月之明，下塞君子之路。

translations.literal: Moreover He Ding was originally a running-footman petty man, beneath menials—his person had not a speck of conduct, his ability not the use of hawk or hound—yet Your Majesty loves his flattery, lends him the handle of authority, so that Ding, relying on favor, gives free rein to himself, arrogates awe and blessing, with his mouth corrects state discussion, with his hand plays with Heaven's mechanism, above injuring the brightness of sun and moon, below blocking the road of gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He Ding was a runner beneath slaves, without a shred of merit—yet you dote on his flattery, hand him power, let him twist state policy and block the path of good men.

sentences.zh: 夫小人求人，必進奸利，定間妄興事役，發江邊戍兵以驅麋鹿，結置山陵，芟夷林莽，殫其九野之獸，聚於重圍之內，上無益時之分，下有損耗之費。

translations.literal: Now petty men who seek from others surely advance treacherous profit; Ding between times rashly raises work projects, sends out riverbank garrison troops to drive elk and deer, sets nets on hills, mows down forests and thickets, exhausts the beasts of the nine wilds and gathers them within heavy enclosures—above there is no share of benefit for the times, below there is harm of waste and expense.
translations.idiomatic: He Ding wastes troops hunting game, strips the hills, pens every beast—no gain to the state, only ruinous cost.

sentences.zh: 而兵士疲於運送，人力竭於驅逐，老弱饑凍，大小怨歎。

translations.literal: And the soldiers are worn out in transport, human strength exhausted in driving; old and young hunger and freeze, great and small cry out in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers stagger under corvée, the people starve and curse.

sentences.zh: 臣竊觀天變，自比年以來陰陽錯謬，四時逆節，日食地震；

translations.literal: Your servant has privately observed Heaven's changes: from these years onward yin and yang are wrong, the four seasons run contrary to rule, there are solar eclipses and earthquakes;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's omens grow strange—yin and yang reversed, seasons awry, eclipses and quakes;

sentences.zh: 中夏隕霜，參之典籍，皆陰氣陵陽，小人弄勢之所致也。

translations.literal: in the central plains frost has fallen; checked against the canons, all are yin overwhelming yang, petty men playing with power.
translations.idiomatic: frost in midsummer—all signs that yin bullies yang while petty men twist power.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗覽書傳，驗諸行事，災祥之應，所為寒慄。

translations.literal: Your servant has once perused documents and books, verified them against deeds done—the response of portents and prodigies is such as to make one cold with fear.
translations.idiomatic: History shows such omens always presage ruin—it chills the blood.

sentences.zh: 昔高宗修己以消鼎雉之異，宋景崇德以退熒惑之變。

translations.literal: In olden times Gaozong cultivated himself to dispel the prodigy of the cauldron and pheasant; Song Jing honored virtue to make Mars's guarding the heart retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong and Duke Jing of Song averted Heaven's wrath by virtue.

sentences.zh: 願陛下上懼皇天譴告之誚，下追二君攘災之道，遠覽前代任賢之功，近寤今日謬授之失，清澄朝位，旌敘俊乂，放退佞邪，抑奪奸勢。

translations.literal: Your servant prays Your Majesty will above fear Heaven's reproving blame, below pursue the two lords' way of warding off disaster, look far to the work of employing the worthy in former ages, wake near to the error of wrong appointments today, clear and settle court posts, raise banners for the outstanding, send away flattery and evil, check and seize treacherous power.
translations.idiomatic: Fear Heaven's warnings, follow those ancient models, purge the court of crooks, and curb corrupt power.

sentences.zh: 如是之輩，一匆復用，廣延淹滯，容受直辭，祗承乾指，敬奉先業，則大化光敷，天人望塞也。

translations.literal: If such as these are not again employed, broadly extend the long-stagnant, accept and hold straight speech, reverently undertake Qian's finger, respectfully uphold the former enterprise—then great transformation will brightly spread and Heaven and man will have their hopes filled.
translations.idiomatic: Welcome the long-excluded, hear blunt truth, honor your father's work—then the realm may heal.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：‘國之興也，視民如赤子。

translations.literal: The Tradition says: "When a state is rising, it looks on the people as a newborn babe.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Tradition says a rising state cherishes the people as infants;

sentences.zh: 其亡也，以民為草芥。

translations.literal: When it perishes, it takes the people as straw and husks.
translations.idiomatic: a dying state treats them as chaff.

sentences.zh: ’陛下昔韜神光，潛德東夏，以聖哲茂姿，龍飛應天，四海延頸，八方拭目，以成康之化必隆於旦夕也。

translations.literal: ' When Your Majesty formerly hid divine radiance and concealed virtue in the eastern lands, with sage and wise abundant bearing, the dragon rose in response to Heaven—within the four seas they stretched their necks, within the eight directions they wiped their eyes, thinking the transformation of Cheng and Kang would surely flourish within a morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: When you lived in the east the realm looked for a Cheng-Kang age the moment you mounted the throne.

sentences.zh: 自登位以來，法禁轉苛，賦調益繁。

translations.literal: Since ascending the seat, legal prohibitions have turned harsher, levies and taxes grown more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Instead, laws grew crueler and taxes heavier.

sentences.zh: 中宮內豎，分佈州郡，橫興事役，競造奸利。

translations.literal: Palace women and eunuchs are spread through the commanderies, rashly raising work projects, competing to create treacherous profit.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs fan out through the provinces, inventing projects and lining their pockets.

sentences.zh: 百姓罹杼軸之困，黎民罷無已之求，老幼饑寒，家戶萊色，而所在長吏，迫畏罪負，嚴法峻刑，苦民求辦。

translations.literal: The hundred surnames suffer the hardship of shuttle and loom; the black-haired people tire of unending demands; old and young hunger and freeze, households show the color of greens; yet the senior officials in each place, pressed and fearing blame, use harsh law and cruel punishments, tormenting the people to seek completion.
translations.idiomatic: The people groan under endless taxes; families go hungry and gray-faced while magistrates, terrified of blame, torture them with harsh law to meet quotas.

sentences.zh: 是以人力不堪，家戶離散，呼嗟之聲，感傷和氣。

translations.literal: Therefore human strength cannot bear it, households scatter and separate, sounds of crying out touch and injure harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Families break apart and wails of despair sour the very air.

sentences.zh: 又江邊戍兵，遠當以拓土廣境，近當以守界備難，宜特優育，以待有事，而征發賦調，煙至雲集，衣不全裋褐，食不瞻朝夕，出當鋒鏑之難，入抱無聊之戚。

translations.literal: Moreover the riverbank garrison troops, in the far case ought to broaden soil and widen borders, in the near case ought to guard the frontier and prepare for difficulty—they ought specially to be favored and nurtured, to await when there is business; yet levies and conscriptions gather thick as smoke and clouds; clothes are not whole in short brown, food does not suffice morning and evening; going out they face the hardship of arrow points, entering they embrace the grief of idleness.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi garrisons need rest to guard the frontier, yet levies swarm like clouds; men lack decent clothes or two meals a day, die on the line, and return to empty homes.

sentences.zh: 是以父子相棄，叛者成行。

translations.literal: Therefore fathers and sons abandon one another, rebels form lines.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers and sons desert each other and deserters line the roads.

sentences.zh: 願陛下寬賦除煩，振恤窮乏，省諸不急，蕩禁約法，則海內樂業，大化普洽。

translations.literal: Your servant prays Your Majesty will widen levies and remove vexations, relieve and pity the destitute, cut all that is not urgent, sweep away prohibitions and simplify the law—then within the seas they will rejoice in their occupations and great transformation will broadly harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Ease taxes, aid the poor, scrap needless projects, and simplify the code—then the realm may live in peace.

sentences.zh: 夫民者國之本，食者民之命也，今國無一年之儲。

translations.literal: Now the people are the state's root, food is the people's life—today the state has not one year's store.
translations.idiomatic: The people are the root; grain is their life—yet the treasury holds less than a year's grain.

sentences.zh: 家無經月之畜，而後宮之中坐食者萬有餘人。

translations.literal: Households have not a month's accumulation, while within the rear palace more than ten thousand sit and eat.
translations.idiomatic: Families lack a month's savings while over ten thousand idlers feast in the harem.

sentences.zh: 內有離曠之怨，外有損耗之費。

translations.literal: Within there is resentment at separation and vacancy; without there is waste and expense.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace women pine in neglect; without, the treasury bleeds.

sentences.zh: 使庫廩空於無用，士民饑於糟糠。

translations.literal: It causes granaries to empty on the useless, gentry and commoners to hunger on husks and chaff.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries drain for no good while the people starve on chaff.

sentences.zh: 又北敵注目，伺國盛衰，陛下不恃己之威德；

translations.literal: Moreover the northern foe fixes his gaze, watching whether the state waxes or wanes; Your Majesty does not rely on your own awe and virtue;
translations.idiomatic: The northern enemy watches our strength; you do not trust your own virtue;

sentences.zh: 而怙敵之不來，忽四海之困窮，而輕虜之不為難，誠非長策廟勝之要也。

translations.literal: yet you rely on the enemy's not coming, neglect the four seas' destitution, and treat the barbarians' not acting as easy—this is truly not the essential of long strategy and temple victory.
translations.idiomatic: you bank on their staying away, ignore the empire's misery, and assume they will never strike—no recipe for lasting victory.

sentences.zh: 昔大皇帝勤身苦體，創基南夏，割據江山，拓士萬里，雖承天贊，實由人力也。

translations.literal: In olden times the Grand Emperor toiled body and suffered flesh, founded the base in southern Xia, carved the rivers and mountains, expanded territory ten thousand li—though he received Heaven's aid, in truth it was by human strength.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Emperor built Wu with his own sweat though Heaven smiled on him.

sentences.zh: 餘慶遺祚，至於陛下，陛下宜勉崇德器，以光前烈。

translations.literal: Remaining blessing and handed-down fortune have reached Your Majesty; Your Majesty ought to strive to honor virtue and capacity, to brighten the former blazing deeds.
translations.idiomatic: His legacy rests with you—honor his virtue and magnify his deeds.

sentences.zh: 愛民養士，保全先軌，何可忽顯祖之功勤，輕難得之大業。

translations.literal: Cherish the people and nurture scholars, preserve intact the former tracks—how can you neglect the Grand Ancestor's toil and slight a hard-won great enterprise?
translations.idiomatic: Cherish the people and the scholar-officials; do not squander what he won with such pain.

sentences.zh: 忘天下之不振，替興衰之巨變哉?臣聞否泰無常，吉兇由人，長江限不可久恃，苟我不守，一葦可航也。

translations.literal: Forget that All-under-Heaven is not rising, replace the great change of rise and fall? Your servant has heard that woe and weal are not constant, fortune and misfortune lie with men; the Yangzi's barrier cannot long be relied on—if we do not guard it, a single reed can be sailed across.
translations.idiomatic: Will you forget the realm's peril? Fortune turns; the Yangzi is no eternal shield—fail to hold it and a reed boat suffices to cross.

sentences.zh: 昔秦建皇帝之號，據殽函之阻，德化不修，法政苛酷，毒流生民，忠臣杜口，是以一夫大呼，社稷傾覆。

translations.literal: In olden times Qin assumed the title of emperor, occupied the barrier of Yao and Han, did not cultivate virtue and transformation, law and government were harsh and cruel, poison flowed to the living people, loyal ministers sealed their mouths—therefore one man shouted aloud and the altars overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Qin held the passes yet fell to one cry of revolt when law turned cruel and loyal tongues fell silent.

sentences.zh: 近劉氏據三關之險，守重山之固，可謂金城石室，萬世之業，任授失賢，一朝喪沒，君臣系頸，共為羈僕。

translations.literal: Recently the Liu house held the peril of three passes, guarded the solidity of layered mountains—it could be called metal walls and stone chambers, an enterprise for ten thousand generations; appointments lost the worthy, in one morning it was lost and sunk, lord and ministers with cords about their necks together became tethered servants.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shan held impregnable Shu yet lost everything in a day when wrong men held office—ruler and ministers bound like slaves.

sentences.zh: 此當世之明鑒，目前之炯戒也。

translations.literal: This is a clear mirror of the age, a blazing warning before the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: That is the mirror of our age and a warning in plain sight.

sentences.zh: 願陛下遠考前事，近覽世變，豐基強本，割情從道，則成康之治興，而聖祖之祚隆矣。

translations.literal: Your servant prays Your Majesty will examine far the former affairs, look near at the changes of the age, fatten the base and strengthen the root, cut private feeling and follow the Way—then the rule of Cheng and Kang will rise and the Grand Ancestor's fortune will flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Study past and present, strengthen the foundations, rule by principle, not whim—then you may revive a Cheng-Kang age and honor your ancestor's line.

sentences.zh: 書奏，皓深恨之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Hao deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao read the memorial and nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 邵奉公貞正，親近所憚。

translations.literal: Shao served the public with integrity and uprightness; those intimate with the ruler feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He Shao was incorrupt and upright—the emperor's favorites feared him.

sentences.zh: 乃共譖邵與樓玄謗毀國事，俱被詰責。

translations.literal: Thereupon they jointly slandered Shao and Lou Xuan as slandering and ruining state affairs; both received edict interrogation and blame.
translations.idiomatic: They framed He Shao and Lou Xuan for defaming the state; both were censured.

sentences.zh: 玄見送南州，邵原復職。

translations.literal: Xuan was seen off to the southern province; Shao was originally restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Xuan went south while He Shao was briefly restored.

sentences.zh: 後邵中惡風，口不能言，去職數月，皓疑其托疾，收付酒藏，掠考千所，邵卒無一語，竟見殺害，家屬徙臨海。

translations.literal: Afterward Shao was struck by evil wind and could not speak; he left office several months; Hao suspected he feigned illness, seized him and handed him to the wine bureau, tortured and examined at a thousand places—Shao to the end had not one word, and in the end was killed; family dependants were moved to Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: He Shao fell mute with a stroke; Sun Hao called it shamming, jailed him in the wine office, tortured him endlessly—He never spoke and was murdered; his kin were banished to Linhai.

sentences.zh: 並下詔誅玄子孫，是歲天冊元年也，邵年四十九。

translations.literal: At the same time an edict went down to execute Xuan's sons and grandsons; it was the first year of the Tiance era; Shao was forty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: The same year Sun Hao ordered Lou Xuan's descendants executed; it was the first year of Tiance; He Shao was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 〈邵子循，字彦先。

translations.literal: Shao's son Xun, courtesy name Yanxian.
translations.idiomatic: His son He Xun, courtesy name Yanxian,

sentences.zh: 虞预晋书曰：循丁家祸，流放海滨，吴平，还乡里。

translations.literal: Yu Yu's Jin shu states: Xun suffered family disaster, was banished to the sea's edge; when Wu was pacified, he returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu's Jin History says He Xun suffered family ruin, was exiled to the coast, and returned home when Wu fell.

sentences.zh: 节操高厉，童

translations.literal: His integrity was high and stern; as a child
translations.idiomatic: High-minded from childhood,

translations.literal: 〈tooth variant〉
translations.idiomatic: (text: fragmentary character in source)

sentences.zh: 不群，言行举动，必以礼让。

translations.literal: he was not of the common herd; in speech and deed he always used ritual yielding.
translations.idiomatic: he stood apart from other boys, always courteous in word and deed.

sentences.zh: 好学博闻，尤善三礼。

translations.literal: He loved learning and read widely, especially skilled in the three ritual canons.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books and excelled in the three ritual classics.

sentences.zh: 举秀子，除阳羡、武康令。

translations.literal: Recommended as flourishing talent, he was appointed magistrate of Yangxian and Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a flourishing talent, he became magistrate of Yangxian and Wukang.

sentences.zh: 顾荣、陆机、陆云表荐循曰：“伏见吴兴武康令贺循德量邃茂，才鉴清远，服膺道素，风操凝峻，历践三城，刑政肃穆，守职下县，编名凡萃，出自新邦，朝无知己，恪居遐外，志不自营，年时倏忽，而邈无阶绪，实州党愚智所为怅然。

translations.literal: Gu Rong, Lu Ji, and Lu Yun submitted a memorial recommending Xun, saying: "We humbly see that He Xun, magistrate of Wukang in Wuxing, has deep and abundant virtue and measure, talent and insight clear and far, embraces the plain of the Way, conduct and integrity stern and lofty; he has passed through three cities in office, punishments and government solemn, guarding duty in a lower county, his name listed among the common mass, coming from a new state, the court without one who knows him, respectfully dwelling far outside, his intent not self-seeking, years and seasons suddenly passing, yet far without ladder or thread—truly what the foolish and wise of the province together feel regret about.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rong, Lu Ji, and Lu Yun jointly memorialized: "He Xun of Wukang combines depth of character with clarity of judgment, lives by the plain Way, and has governed three counties with a stern hand. A man of a newly conquered land without patrons at court, he languishes in a minor post while years slip away—the whole province grieves to see talent wasted."

sentences.zh: 臣等并以凡才，累授饰进，被服恩泽，忝豫朝末，知良士后时，而守局无言，惧有蔽贤之咎，是以不胜愚管，谨冒死表闻。

translations.literal: We your servants are all with ordinary talent, repeatedly receiving advancement in ornament, clothed in favor and grace, shamefully placed at the court's end; knowing a good gentleman is behind the times yet guarding our posts without speech, we fear the fault of concealing the worthy—therefore, unable to bear our foolish tubes, we respectfully risk death to set forth and be heard.
translations.idiomatic: We are mediocre men already favored at court; to stay silent while a worthy languishes would be to hide talent from you—we therefore risk death to speak."

sentences.zh: ”久之，召为太子舍人。

translations.literal: " After a long time he was summoned to be attendant to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After long delay he was named attendant to the heir apparent."

sentences.zh: 石冰破扬州，循亦合众，事平，杜门不出。

translations.literal: When Shi Bing broke Yangzhou, Xun also gathered a host; when the affair was settled, he closed his door and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Bing ravaged Yangzhou, He Xun raised troops; when peace returned he shut his gates and would not show himself.

sentences.zh: 陈敏作乱，以循为丹杨内史，循称疾固辞，敏不敢逼。

translations.literal: When Chen Min rebelled, he appointed Xun as interior administrator of Danyang; Xun claimed illness and firmly declined—Min did not dare force him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min tried to name him interior administrator of Danyang; He Xun pleaded illness and Chen Min dared not press him.

sentences.zh: 于时江东豪右无不受敏爵位，惟循与同郡硃诞不挂贼网。

translations.literal: At that time among the powerful families east of the Yangzi none did not accept titles from Min—only Xun together with Zhu Dan of his commandery did not hang in the rebel's net.
translations.idiomatic: While every great clan in Jiangdong took Chen Min's commissions, only He Xun and his townsman Zhu Dan refused the rebel's snare.

sentences.zh: 后除吴国内史，不就。

translations.literal: Afterward he was appointed interior administrator of Wu commandery but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was later offered interior administrator of Wu but declined.

sentences.zh: 元皇帝为镇东将军，请循为军司马，帝为晋王，以循为中书令，固让不受，转太常，领太子太傅。

translations.literal: When Prince Yuan was general who guards the east, he requested Xun as army marshal; when the Prince became Prince of Jin, he made Xun director of the secretariat—he firmly declined and would not accept, was transferred to grand master of ceremonies, concurrently grand tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui was general who guards the east he asked He Xun to be his army marshal; as Prince of Jin he offered the secretariat—He Xun refused—and made him grand master of ceremonies and grand tutor to the heir apparent instead.

sentences.zh: 时朝廷初建，动有疑议，宗庙制度皆循所定，朝野谘询，为一时儒宗。

translations.literal: At that time the court was newly established; whenever there was doubt in discussion, the rites of the ancestral temple were all what Xun settled; court and wild consulted him—he was the Confucian leader of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the new Jin court he settled every disputed ritual and became the age's leading Confucian authority.

sentences.zh: 年六十，太兴二年卒。

translations.literal: At age sixty he died in the second year of Taixing.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty in the second year of Taixing (321).

sentences.zh: 追赠司空，谥曰穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was honored as minister of works, posthumous name Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named minister of works with the posthumous epithet Mu.

sentences.zh: 循诸所著论，并传於世。

translations.literal: The various treatises Xun wrote were all transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His essays survive in his collected works.

sentences.zh: 子隰，临海太守。〉

translations.literal: His son Xi was grand administrator of Linhai."
translations.idiomatic: His son He Xi became grand administrator of Linhai."

sentences.zh: 韋曜字弘嗣，吳郡雲陽人也。

translations.literal: Wei Yao, courtesy name Hongsi, was a man of Yunyang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao, courtesy name Hongsi, came from Yunyang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈曜本名昭，史为晋讳，改之。〉

translations.literal: Yao's original given name was Zhao; the histories avoid the Jin taboo and changed it."
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Wei Zhao; historians changed it to Yao to avoid the Jin taboo on "Zhao."

sentences.zh: 少好學，能屬文，從丞相掾除西安令，還為尚書郎，遷太子中庶子。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, could compose texts; from aide to the chancellor he was appointed magistrate of Xi'an, returned as gentleman of the masters of writing, was promoted to palace attendant to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and prose, rose from chancellor's aide to magistrate of Xi'an, then gentleman of the secretariat and palace attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 時蔡穎亦在東宮，性好博奕。

translations.literal: At that time Cai Ying was also in the Eastern Palace and by nature loved board games.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ying shared the heir's household and loved weiqi.

sentences.zh: 太子和以為無益，命曜論之。

translations.literal: The heir apparent He thought it without benefit and ordered Yao to discourse on it.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince He judged it a waste and asked Wei Yao to write against it.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: His words said:
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao wrote:

sentences.zh: 蓋聞君子恥當年而功不立，疾設世而名不稱，故曰‘學如不及，猶恐失之’。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the gentleman is ashamed if in his year merit is not established, grieved if in the established age his name is not praised—therefore it is said 'Study as if you could not catch up, and still fear to lose it.'
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman hates to reach year's end without achievement or age without a good name—hence the saying, "Study as if you could never catch up, and still fear to fall behind."

sentences.zh: 是以古之志士，悼年齒之流邁而懼名稱之不立也，故逸精厲操，晨興夜寐，不遑寧息，經之以歲月，累之以日力，若寧越之勤，董生之篤，漸漬德義之淵，棲遲道藝之域。

translations.literal: Therefore the determined scholars of old mourned the flowing away of years and teeth and feared that reputation would not be established; therefore they exhausted essence and sharpened conduct, rose early and slept late, had no leisure for rest, threaded it with years and months, piled it with daily strength—like Ning Yue's diligence, Dong Zhongshu's earnestness, gradually steeping in the deep of virtue and righteousness, lingering in the field of the Way and arts.
translations.idiomatic: So the worthies of old mourned passing years and sharpened body and mind—like Ning Yue or Dong Zhongshu—wading deep into the classics.

sentences.zh: 且以西伯之聖，姬公之才，猶有日昃待旦之勞，故能隆興周道，垂名億載，況在臣庶，而可以已乎？

translations.literal: Moreover with the West Lord's sagehood and the Duke of Zhou's talent, they still had the toil of the sun slanting while waiting for dawn—therefore they could raise and flourish the Zhou Way and hang their names for a hundred million ages; how much more among ministers and commoners—can one stop?
translations.idiomatic: Even King Wen and the Duke of Zhou toiled past sunset to build Zhou's fame—how can lesser men slacken?

sentences.zh: 歷觀古今功名之士，皆有累積殊異之跡，勞身苦體，契闊勤思，平居不墮其業，窮困不易其素，是以卜式立志於耕牧，而黃霸受道於囹圄，終有榮顯之福，以成不朽之名。

translations.literal: Looking through past and present men of achievement and fame, all have tracks piled up and extraordinary; they toiled body and suffered flesh, were earnest in hardship and thought; in ordinary life they did not drop their calling, in destitution they did not alter their plainness—therefore Bu Shi set his will in plowing and herding, while Huang Ba received the Way in prison, and in the end had blessing of glory and display, thereby completing an indestructible name.
translations.idiomatic: Every great name rests on relentless effort—Bu Shi from the plow, Huang Ba from a jail cell—until glory crowns their constancy.

sentences.zh: 故山甫勤於夙夜，而吳漢不離公門，豈有遊惰哉？

translations.literal: Therefore Shanfu was diligent from dawn to night, and Wu Han did not leave the public gate—could there be wandering laziness?
translations.idiomatic: Shanfu labored night and day; Wu Han never left the yamen—were they idle?

sentences.zh: 今世之人多不務經術，好玩博奕，廢事棄業，忘寢與食，窮日盡明，繼以脂燭。

translations.literal: People of the present age for the most part do not devote themselves to the classics and arts, but love to play board games, abandon tasks and cast aside calling, forget sleep and food, exhaust the day to the limit of light, then continue with lamp fat.
translations.idiomatic: Today men shun the classics for weiqi, skip meals and work, and play by candlelight.

sentences.zh: 當其臨局交爭，雌雄未決，專精銳意，心勞體倦，人事曠而不修，賓旅闕而不接，雖有太牢之饌，《韶》、《夏》之樂，不暇存也。

translations.literal: When they face the board and contend, winner not yet decided, they fix mind and sharpen intent, heart wearies and body tires; human affairs are left vast and untended, guests and travelers are lacking and not received—though there be a grand feast, though there be Shao and Xia music, they have no leisure to notice.
translations.idiomatic: At the board they ignore guests, state, even feasts and court music.

sentences.zh: 至或賭及衣物，徙棋易行，廉恥之意弛，而忿戾之色發，然其所志不出一枰之上，所務不過方罫之間，勝敵無封爵之賞，獲地無兼土之實，技非六藝，用非經國。

translations.literal: Even to staking clothes, moving pieces and changing lines, the sense of modesty and shame relaxes and looks of anger and harshness appear; yet what they aim at does not go beyond one board, what they strive at does not pass between the squares—defeating the enemy brings no fief reward, capturing ground yields no doubled territory; the skill is not of the six arts, the use is not for ordering the state.
translations.idiomatic: They wager clothes, lose temper, and win neither rank nor land—the skill is not among the six arts nor fit to rule a state.

sentences.zh: 立身者不階其術，徵選者不由其道。

translations.literal: Those who establish themselves do not climb by this art; those summoned for selection do not go by this path.
translations.idiomatic: Office seekers do not rise by the board; selectors do not test it.

sentences.zh: 求之於戰陳，則非孫、吳之倫也。

translations.literal: Seek it in battle array—it is not of the class of Sun and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: It is no art of war like Sun Wu's.

sentences.zh: 考之於道藝，則非孔氏之門也；

translations.literal: Examine it in the Way and arts—it is not of Confucius's gate;
translations.idiomatic: It is not Confucian learning;

sentences.zh: 以變詐為務，則非忠信之士也；

translations.literal: take shifting deceit as the task—it is not of loyal and trustworthy gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: it breeds cunning, not loyalty;

sentences.zh: 以劫殺為名，則非仁者之意也；

translations.literal: take robbery and killing as the name—it is not of the intent of the humane;
translations.idiomatic: it teaches rapacity, not benevolence;

sentences.zh: 而空妨日廢業，終無補益。

translations.literal: yet vainly it hinders days and wastes calling, and in the end has no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: yet it wastes days to no profit.

sentences.zh: 是何異設木而擊之，置石而投之哉！

translations.literal: How is this different from setting up a post and striking it, placing a stone and casting at it!
translations.idiomatic: What better than beating a stake or throwing stones?

sentences.zh: 且君子之居室也勤身以致養，其在朝也竭命以納忠，臨事且猶旰食，而何博奕之足耽？

translations.literal: Moreover the gentleman's dwelling is to toil the body to bring nurture; in court he exhausts life to offer loyalty; facing affairs he still eats at noon—how can board games be worth addiction?
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman toils at home and serves in court—how can games deserve addiction?

sentences.zh: 夫然，故孝友之行立，貞純之名彰也。

translations.literal: If it is so, then the conduct of filial piety and brotherhood is established, and the name of chaste purity is displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Then filial duty shines and a clean name endures.

sentences.zh: 方今大吳受命，海內未平，聖朝乾乾，務在得人，勇略之士則受熊虎之任，儒雅之徒則處龍鳳之署，百行兼苞，文武並騖，博選良才，旌簡髦俊。

translations.literal: Now great Wu has received the mandate, within the seas is not yet pacified, the sage court is diligent, the task lies in obtaining men—men of courage and strategy then receive bear-and-tiger posts, men of elegant learning then sit in dragon-and-phoenix offices; the hundred conducts are together embraced, civil and martial both race; broadly select good talent, raise banners for the outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Wu must win worthy men—warriors for tiger posts, scholars for phoenix halls—choose widely and lift the best.

sentences.zh: 設程式之科，垂金爵之賞，誠千載之嘉會，百世之良遇也，當世之士，宜勉思至道，愛功惜力，以佐明時，使名書史籍，勳在盟府，乃君子之上務，當今之先急也。

translations.literal: Set up graded examinations, hang rewards of gold and noble rank—truly a fine meeting of a thousand ages, a good encounter of a hundred generations; gentlemen of the age ought to strive to think on the utmost Way, cherish achievement and spare strength, to assist the bright times, causing their names to be written in the histories and their merit in the covenant house—this is the gentleman's highest task and the present's foremost urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Open exams and rich rewards—then scholars should bend their minds to the Way, win fame in the histories, and aid the throne—that is the true calling.

sentences.zh: 夫一木之枰孰與方國之封？

translations.literal: Now one wooden board—how does it compare to a fief over a region?
translations.idiomatic: One wooden board—how does it weigh against a border fief?

sentences.zh: 枯棋三百孰與萬人之將?兗龍之服，金石之樂，足以兼棋局而貿博弈矣。

translations.literal: Three hundred withered pieces—how does it compare to a general of ten thousand men? Robes of nine dragons, music of metal and stone are enough to trade a board for and barter away board games.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred stones against command of ten thousand—imperial robes and bell music outweigh any game.

sentences.zh: 假令世士移博奕之力而用之於詩書，是有顏、閔之志也。

translations.literal: Suppose gentlemen of the age shifted the strength spent on board games and used it on the Odes and documents—then they would have the will of Yan and Min.
translations.idiomatic: Turn that zeal to the classics and you approach Yan Hui and Min Ziqian;

sentences.zh: 用之於智計，是有良、平之思也。

translations.literal: use it on stratagem—then they would have the thought of Liang and Ping.
translations.idiomatic: turn it to strategy and you think like Zhang Liang and Chen Ping;

sentences.zh: 用之於資貨，是有猗頓之富也；

translations.literal: use it on goods and wealth—then they would have the riches of Yi Dun;
translations.idiomatic: turn it to trade and you grow rich as Yi Dun;

sentences.zh: 用之於射御，是有將帥之備也。

translations.literal: use it on archery and charioteering—then they would have the readiness of generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: turn it to archery and chariotry and you train commanders.

sentences.zh: 如此則功名立而鄙賤遠矣。

translations.literal: If so, then achievement and fame are established and baseness is kept far.
translations.idiomatic: Do this and honor nears while vulgarity recedes.

sentences.zh: 和廢後，為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: After He was deposed, he became gentleman attendant at the yellow gates.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince He's deposition Wei Yao became gentleman attendant at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: 孫亮即位，諸葛恪輔政，表曜為太史令，撰《吳書》，華核、薛瑩等皆與參同，孫休踐阼，為中書郎、博士祭酒。

translations.literal: When Sun Liang ascended the throne, Zhuge Ke governed and memorialized Yao as grand astrologer to compose the Book of Wu; Hua He, Xue Ying, and others all joined in the same work; when Sun Xun mounted the steps, he was gentleman of the secretariat and libationer of erudits.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Liang had Zhuge Ke name him grand astrologer for the Book of Wu; under Sun Xun he was gentleman of the secretariat and chief erudit.

sentences.zh: 命曜依劉向故事，校定眾書。

translations.literal: He ordered Yao according to Liu Xiang's precedent to collate and fix the multitude of books.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xun ordered him to collate the imperial library on Liu Xiang's model.

sentences.zh: 又欲延曜侍講，而左將軍張布近習寵幸，事行多玷，憚曜侍講儒士，又性精確，懼以古今警戒休意，固爭不可。

translations.literal: He also wished to extend Yao as lecturer-in-waiting, but General of the Left Zhang Bu was a near attendant, favored and doted on, his deeds many times stained; he feared Yao as lecturer, a Confucian gentleman, and moreover by nature precise, feared he would use past and present to warn Xun's intent—therefore he firmly contended that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He wished Wei Yao to lecture the throne, but Zhang Bu, the favorite general, blocked it, fearing a scholar would lecture Sun Xun on moral history.

sentences.zh: 休深恨布，語在《休傳》。

translations.literal: Xun deeply hated Bu—the words are in the biography of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xun came to hate Zhang Bu—the story is told in Sun Xun's biography.

sentences.zh: 然曜竟止不入。

translations.literal: Yet in the end Yao stopped and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao never took the lecturer's post.

sentences.zh: 孫皓即位，封高陵亭侯，遷中書僕射，職省，為侍中，常領左國史。

translations.literal: When Sun Hao ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Gaoling, promoted to vice director of the secretariat; when the office was cut, he became attendant within, normally holding the post of left state historian.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao enfeoffed him at Gaoling, made him vice director of the secretariat, then attendant within and left state historian.

sentences.zh: 時所在承指數言瑞應。

translations.literal: At that time each place, carrying out hints, repeatedly spoke of auspicious responses.
translations.idiomatic: Every district reported bogus omens to please the throne.

sentences.zh: 皓以問曜，曜答曰：“此人家筐篋中物耳。

translations.literal: Hao used this to ask Yao; Yao answered saying: "These are things in people's household baskets and boxes, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao asked; Wei Yao answered, "Those are trinkets any household could fake.

sentences.zh: ”又皓欲為父和作紀，曜執以和不登帝位，宜名為傳。

translations.literal: " Moreover Hao wished to make a annals for his father He; Yao insisted that because He did not ascend the imperial seat, it ought to be titled biography.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao wanted annals for his father Prince He; Wei Yao insisted on a mere biography because He never ruled.

sentences.zh: 如是者非一，漸見責怒。

translations.literal: Matters like this were not one; gradually he met blame and anger.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the emperor again and again and drew mounting wrath.

sentences.zh: 曜益憂懼，自陳衰老，求去侍、史二官，乞欲成所造書，以從業別有所付，皓終不聽。

translations.literal: Yao grew more anxious and fearful, stated himself old and declining, begged to leave the two offices of attendant and historian, begged to be allowed to finish the books he was composing, so that the work might be handed to another—Hao in the end would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded age and asked to resign as historian and finish his books—Sun Hao refused.

sentences.zh: 時有疾病，醫藥監護，持之愈急。

translations.literal: At times he had illness; medical care and supervision held him ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, Sun Hao hemmed him in with doctors and guards.

sentences.zh: 皓每饗宴，無不竟日，坐席無能否率以七升為限，雖不悉入口，皆澆灌取盡。

translations.literal: Whenever Hao feasted, it was never less than the whole day; those seated, whether capable or not, were all limited to seven sheng—even if not all entered the mouth, they poured and washed until finished.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao's feasts ran all day with a seven-sheng quota for every guest, poured down whether drunk or not.

sentences.zh: 曜素飲酒不過二升，初見禮異時，常為裁減，或密賜茶荈以當酒，至於寵衰，更見逼強，輒以為罪。

translations.literal: Yao by nature drank no more than two sheng of wine; at first when treated with special courtesy, they often reduced the measure for him, or secretly bestowed tea for herbs in place of wine; when favor waned, he met more forced pressure, and that was always taken as a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao could barely drink two sheng; at first Sun Hao cut his ration or slipped him tea, then forced the full cup and called refusal a crime.

sentences.zh: 又於酒後使侍臣難折公卿，以嘲弄侵克發摘私短以為歡。

translations.literal: Moreover after wine he ordered attendant ministers to press and break dukes and ministers, using mockery, encroachment, and picking private faults as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: After wine Sun Hao made attendants bait ministers, mock them, and expose private faults for sport.

sentences.zh: 時有衍過，或誤犯皓諱，輒見收縛，至於誅戮。

translations.literal: At times there were slips of the tongue, or by mistake one violated Hao's taboo—immediately they were seized and bound, even to execution and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: A slip of tongue or a taboo word meant arrest and often death.

sentences.zh: 曜以為外相毀傷，內長尤恨，使不濟濟，非佳事也，故但示難問經義言論而已。

translations.literal: Yao thought that outward mutual tearing down and inward growth of blame and hatred, making the host not stately, was not a fine affair; therefore he only showed hard questions on canonical meaning and discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao offered dry textual debate instead of public humiliation, thinking shame no way to run a court.

sentences.zh: 皓以為不承用詔命，意不忠盡，遂積前後嫌忿，收曜付獄，是歲鳳皇二年也。

translations.literal: Hao thought he did not carry out and use the edict's command, his intent not loyal to the utmost; thereupon he piled former and later resentments, seized Yao and handed him to prison—it was the second year of Fenghuang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao called that disloyalty, piled old grudges, and jailed him in the second year of Fenghuang (273).

sentences.zh: 曜因獄吏上辭曰：

translations.literal: Yao through the prison clerk submitted a petition saying:
translations.idiomatic: From prison Wei Yao wrote:

sentences.zh: 囚荷恩見哀，無與為比，曾無芒氂有以上報，孤辱恩寵，自陷極罪。

translations.literal: The prisoner has received favor and been pitied—none may compare; never a hair's tip to repay above; alone he has disgraced favor and grace and trapped himself in the utmost crime.
translations.idiomatic: Your prisoner has received undeserved grace and repaid nothing; he has shamed your kindness and earned death.

sentences.zh: 念當灰滅。

translations.literal: He thinks he will be ash and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: He expects to be dust and ashes,

sentences.zh: 長棄黃泉，愚情慺慺，竊有所懷，貪令上聞。

translations.literal: long cast off in the yellow springs; his foolish feeling is earnest; he privately has something in his breast and greedily wishes it heard above.
translations.idiomatic: forever lost under the yellow springs—yet he begs one last hearing for what weighs on his heart.

sentences.zh: 囚昔見世間有古歷注，其所記載既多虛無，在書籍者亦復錯謬。

translations.literal: Your servant formerly saw in the world an old calendar commentary; what it recorded was mostly empty and false, and what was in books was likewise wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In old calendar glosses I found much that was fanciful or plainly wrong.

sentences.zh: 囚尋按傳記，考合異同，採摭耳目所及。

translations.literal: Your servant thereupon searched records and annals, examined and combined differences and samenesses, gathered what ears and eyes reached.
translations.idiomatic: I combed histories, compared variants, and set down what I could verify.

sentences.zh: 以作《洞紀》，紀自庖犧，至於秦、漢，凡為三卷，當起黃武以來，別作一卷，事尚未成。

translations.literal: To compose the Tong ji, chronicling from Paoxi down to Qin and Han, in all three rolls; from the rise of Huangwu onward separately to compose one roll—the work is not yet finished.
translations.idiomatic: I wrote the Tong ji in three scrolls from Paoxi through Qin and Han, and planned a fourth from Huangwu—unfinished.

sentences.zh: 又見劉熙所作《釋名》，信多佳者，然物類眾多，難得詳究。

translations.literal: Moreover he saw the Shi ming composed by Liu Xi—truly many fine points, yet the kinds of things are numerous and hard to exhaust in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xi's Shi ming has many fine entries, yet the categories are vast and hard to perfect.

sentences.zh: 故時有得失，而爵位之事，又有非是。

translations.literal: Therefore at times there are gains and losses, and in matters of ranks and offices there are also errors.
translations.idiomatic: Some glosses are wrong, especially on offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 愚以官爵，今之所急，不宜乘誤。

translations.literal: Your servant considers offices and noble ranks what the present urgently needs—one ought not ride on mistakes.
translations.idiomatic: Titles are too vital to leave uncorrected.

sentences.zh: 囚自忘至微，又作《官職訓》及《辯釋名》各一卷，欲表上之。

translations.literal: Your servant, forgetting his utmost lowliness, moreover composed the Guanzhi xun and the Bian Shi ming, one roll each, desiring to memorialize them upward.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore drafted the Guanzhi xun and Bian Shi ming, one scroll each, for your archives.

sentences.zh: 新寫始畢，會以無狀，幽囚特命，泯沒之日，恨不上聞。

translations.literal: Fresh copying had just been finished, when because of unworthy conduct he was imprisoned on special order; on the day of extinction and drowning, he regretted not being heard above.
translations.idiomatic: The fair copy was barely done when I was jailed—now I may die without laying it before you.

sentences.zh: 謹以先死列狀，乞上言秘府，於外料取，呈內以聞。

translations.literal: Respectfully, before death, he sets forth this petition, begging that it be spoken to the secret archive, that from outside materials be gathered and presented within to be heard.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you send this to the secretariat and have the texts fetched from my lodgings.

sentences.zh: 迫懼淺蔽，不合天聽，抱怖雀息，乞垂哀省。

translations.literal: Pressed and fearful, shallow and blocked, not matching Heaven's hearing, hugging terror and sparrow's breath, he begs pity and inspection.
translations.idiomatic: I tremble at troubling your ears—yet I beg a moment's mercy.

sentences.zh: 曜冀以此求免，而皓更怪其書之垢故，又以詰曜。

translations.literal: Yao hoped by this to seek pardon, but Hao further wondered at the grime on his books and again used it to interrogate Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao thought the smudged manuscripts a new crime and questioned him again.

sentences.zh: 曜對曰：“囚撰此書，實欲表上，懼有誤謬，數數省讀，不覺點污。

translations.literal: Yao answered saying: "Your servant composed this book truly intending to memorialize it upward; fearing there might be error, he repeatedly read it over and did not notice smudges.
translations.idiomatic: I smudged the pages proofreading—I meant to present the work, not to slight you.

sentences.zh: 被問寒戰，形氣吶吃，謹追辭叩頭五百下，兩手自搏。

translations.literal: Questioned, he shivered with cold, form and breath stammered; respectfully he pursues his words, knocking head five hundred times, two hands striking himself.
translations.idiomatic: I stammer in terror and beat my head five hundred times with my own fists.

sentences.zh: ”而華核連上疏救曜曰：

translations.literal: " Yet Hua He repeatedly submitted memorials to rescue Yao, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Hua He then sent a string of memorials for Wei Yao:

sentences.zh: 曜運值千載，特蒙哀識，以其儒學，得與史官，貂蟬內侍，承答天問，聖朝仁篤，慎終追遠，迎神之際，垂涕敕曜。

translations.literal: Yao's fate met a thousand ages, especially receiving pity and recognition; because of his Confucian learning he was allowed to join the historians, sable-collar attendant within, answering Heaven's questions; the sage court is humane and earnest, careful of endings and mindful of the distant; at the meeting to welcome the spirits he wept and ordered Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao rose by scholarship to the historian's desk and answered the throne in the inner court; our late ruler wept when spirits were welcomed and charged Wei Yao with the histories.

sentences.zh: 曜愚惑不達。

translations.literal: Yao was foolish and confused, not penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: He was slow to grasp your intent.

sentences.zh: 不能敷宣陛下大舜之美，而拘擊史官，使聖趣不敘，至行不彰，實曜愚蔽當死之罪，然臣慺慺，見曜自少勤學，雖老不倦，探綜墳典，溫故知新，及意所經識古今行事，外吏之中少過曜者。

translations.literal: He could not spread and proclaim Your Majesty's beauty like great Shun, yet was bound as historian, causing sage intent not to be narrated and utmost conduct not to be displayed—truly Yao's foolish blindness is a crime deserving death; yet your servant earnestly sees that Yao from youth studied diligently, though old not weary, delved into the tomb classics, reviewed the old and knew the new, and in what his mind has passed through, knowledge of past and present deeds—among outer clerks few surpass Yao.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to hymn your Shun-like virtue—yet among field officials none knows the classics like Wei Yao.

sentences.zh: 昔李陵為漢將，軍敗不還而降匈奴，司馬遷不加疾惡，為陵遊說，漢武帝以遷有良史之才，欲使畢成所撰，忍不加誅，書卒成立，垂之無窮。

translations.literal: In olden times Li Ling was a Han general; his army was defeated, did not return, and surrendered to the Xiongnu—Sima Qian did not add harsh hatred and spoke for Ling; Han Wudi, because Qian had talent for a good historian, wished to let him complete what he was writing, bore not to add execution—the book in the end was completed and hangs endless.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wudi spared Sima Qian so the Records could be finished—Li Ling's fall did not cost the historian his life.

sentences.zh: 今曜在吳，亦漢之史遷也。

translations.literal: Now Yao in Wu is also Han's Sima Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao is Wu's Sima Qian.

sentences.zh: 伏見前後符瑞彰著。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly sees that before and after, talisman auspices have been manifest.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen bright omens fore and aft.

sentences.zh: 神指天應，繼出累見，一統之期，庶不復久。

translations.literal: The spirit points, Heaven responds; they have come forth repeatedly in succession—the time of unification, perhaps, will not again be long.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven answers the throne—the day of unification cannot be far.

sentences.zh: 事乎之後，當觀時設制，三王不相因禮，五帝不相沿樂，質文殊塗，損益異體，宜得輩依準古義，有所改立。

translations.literal: After affairs are settled, one ought to observe the times and set institutions; the three kings did not inherit one another's rites, the five emperors did not continue one another's music—substance and pattern differ in path, decrease and increase differ in body—one ought to get a group to take ancient meaning as standard and have places to change and establish.
translations.idiomatic: When peace comes you must reform rites and music as kings of old did—let scholars take the classics as your guide.

sentences.zh: 漢氏承秦，則有叔孫通定一代之儀，曜之才學亦漢通之次也。

translations.literal: The Han house inherited Qin, then there was Shusun Tong who fixed a generation's observances—Yao's talent and learning are next after Han's Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao could be another Shusun Tong for this dynasty.

sentences.zh: 又《吳書》雖已有頭角，敘贊未述。

translations.literal: Moreover the Book of Wu, though it already has horns and head, narrative and praise are not yet set forth.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu has a skeleton but lacks full narrative and appraisal.

sentences.zh: 昔班固作《漢書》，文辭典雅，後劉珍，劉毅等作《漢記》，遠不及固，敘傳尤劣。

translations.literal: In olden times Ban Gu made the Han shu, literary phrasing classic and elegant; afterward Liu Zhen and Liu Yi and others made the Han ji, far not reaching Gu, especially narrative and biography inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's Han shu towers over Liu Zhen's Han ji—the latter's biographies are poor stuff.

sentences.zh: 今年《吳書》當垂千載，編次諸吏，後之才士論次善惡，非得良才如曜者，實不可使闕不朽之書。

translations.literal: Now this year the Book of Wu is to hang for a thousand ages; compiling and ordering the various clerks, later men of talent ordering good and evil—if one does not get a good talent like Yao, truly one cannot let the book of indestructibility lack.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu history must last a millennium—without a talent like Wei Yao it cannot be perfected.

sentences.zh: 如臣頑蔽，誠非其人。

translations.literal: As your servant is stubborn and blocked, truly he is not that man.
translations.idiomatic: I am too dull for the task myself.

sentences.zh: 曜年已七十，餘數無幾，乞赦其一等之罪，為終身徒，使成書業，水足傳未，垂之百世。

translations.literal: Yao's years are already seventy; the remainder of his tally is not much—your servant begs to pardon his crime of one degree, make him a lifelong convict, let him complete the book enterprise, enough to transmit to the future, hang for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: He is seventy—commute his death to lifelong penal labor so he may finish the histories.

sentences.zh: 謹通進表，叩頭百下。

translations.literal: Respectfully he passes forward the memorial, knocking head one hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: I kowtow one hundred times as I send this plea.

sentences.zh: 皓不許，遂誅曜，徙百家零陵。

translations.literal: Hao did not consent, thereupon executed Yao, moved the hundred families to Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao refused, executed Wei Yao, and banished his clan to Lingling.

sentences.zh: 子隆，亦有文學也。

translations.literal: His son Long also had literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei Long was a scholar too.

sentences.zh: 華核字永先，吳郡武進人也。
