translations.literal: Hua He, courtesy name Yongxian, was a man of Wujin in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hua He, courtesy name Yongxian, came from Wujin in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 始為上虞尉、曲農都尉，以文學入為秘府郎，遷中書丞。

translations.literal: At first he was magistrate of Shangyu and commandant of curved agriculture, entered by literary learning as gentleman of the secret archive, was promoted secretariat aide.
translations.idiomatic: He began as magistrate of Shangyu and agricultural commandant, then entered the secret archive and rose to secretariat aide.

sentences.zh: 蜀為魏所並，核詣宮門發表曰：“間聞賊眾蟻聚向西境，西境艱險，謂當無虞。

translations.literal: When Shu was swallowed by Wei, He went to the palace gate and issued a memorial saying: "Lately I heard the bandit host swarms like ants gathering toward the western border; the western border is steep and perilous—I thought there would be no worry.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei conquered Shu, Hua He rushed to the palace gate: "I heard the victors mass on our western frontier; I thought our rugged west would hold—

sentences.zh: 定聞陸抗表至，成都不守，臣主播越，社稷傾覆。

translations.literal: Soon I heard Lu Kang's memorial arrived—Chengdu did not hold, lord and ministers are cast adrift, altars overturned.
translations.idiomatic: then Lu Kang's dispatch came: Chengdu has fallen, ruler and ministers scattered, the dynasty lost."

sentences.zh: 昔衛為翟所滅而桓公存之，今道里長遠，不可救振，失委附之土，棄貢獻之國，臣以草芥，竊懷不寧。

translations.literal: In olden times Wei was destroyed by the Di yet Duke Huan preserved it; now the road is long and far, cannot be rescued and raised; we lose the land that leaned on us, cast away the state that paid tribute—your servant, grass and dust, privately harbors unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Wei once fell to the Di yet Duke Huan of Qi saved it; Shu is too far to save—we lose a shield state and a tributary—I, a mere clerk, tremble for Wu.

sentences.zh: 陛下聖仁，恩澤遠撫，卒聞如此，必垂哀悼。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is sage and humane, favor spreads far in soothing; suddenly hearing thus, surely will let fall mourning pity.
translations.idiomatic: You are merciful—this news must wound you.

sentences.zh: 臣不勝忡悵之情，謹拜表以聞。”

translations.literal: Your servant cannot bear the feeling of anxious grief; respectfully he bows the memorial to be heard."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear my grief and submit this memorial."

sentences.zh: 孫皓即位，封徐陵亭侯。

translations.literal: When Sun Hao ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Xuling.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao took the throne, Hua He was enfeoffed as village marquis of Xuling.

sentences.zh: 實鼎二年，皓更營新宮，制度弘廣，飾以珠玉，所費甚多。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, Hao further built a new palace; the system was vast and broad, ornamented with pearl and jade, the expense very great.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding Sun Hao raised a new palace on a vast plan, inlaid with jade and pearl at ruinous cost.

sentences.zh: 是時盛夏興工，農守並廢，核上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: It was then midsummer and works were raised; farming and garrison both ceased; He submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Midsummer brought corvée that idled farms and garrisons; Hua He remonstrated:

sentences.zh: 臣聞漢文之世，九州晏然，秦民喜去慘毒之苛政，歸劉氏之寬仁，省役約法，與之更始，分王子弟以藩漢室，當此之時，皆以為泰山之安，無窮之基之也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in the age of Han Wen, within the nine provinces it was tranquil; Qin people rejoiced to leave cruel poison of harsh government and return to Liu's lenient benevolence, reduced labor and simplified law, with them made a fresh start, divided kings among sons and younger brothers to screen the Han house—at that time all thought it Mount Tai's peace, base without end.
translations.idiomatic: They thought Han stability eternal as Mount Tai when Wen eased Qin's cruelty.

sentences.zh: 至於賈誼，獨以為可痛哭及流涕者三，可為長歎息者六，乃曰當今之勢何異抱火積薪之下而寢其上，火末及然而謂之安。

translations.literal: As for Jia Yi, alone he thought there were three things fit for bitter crying and flowing tears, six things fit for long sighing—then he said the present situation was no different from hugging fire piled under kindling and sleeping on top; the fire's end had not yet reached yet they called it safe.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi alone warned of sleeping on a pile of kindling.

sentences.zh: 其後變亂，皆如其言。

translations.literal: Afterward changes and rebellion were all as his words.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion followed exactly as he predicted.

sentences.zh: 臣雖下愚，不識大倫，竊以囊時之事，揆今之勢。

translations.literal: Your servant, though lowest foolish, does not know the great norm, privately takes affairs of the bag-time and measures the present situation.
translations.idiomatic: I am a dull man, yet I weigh our age against his.

sentences.zh: 誼曰復數年間，諸王方剛，漢之傅相稱疾罷歸，欲以此為治，雖堯、舜不能安。

translations.literal: Yi said within a few more years the various kings would be in their prime, Han's tutors and chancellors would claim illness and retire—if with this one wished to govern, though Yao and Shun could not bring peace.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi feared young princes and idle tutors—no Yao could govern so.

sentences.zh: 今大敵據九州之地，有大半之眾，習攻戰之餘術，乘戎刀之舊勢，欲與中國爭相吞之計，其猶楚漢勢不兩立，非徒漢之諸王淮南，濟北而已。

translations.literal: Now the great enemy occupies the land of the nine provinces, has more than half the host, is practiced in the leftover arts of attack warfare, rides the old momentum of weapons and blades, wishes with the central states mutually to swallow in planning—it is as Chu and Han with power not two-established, not merely Han's various kings Huainan and Jibei alone.
translations.idiomatic: Our foe holds most of China, veteran in war—this is no mere Huainan revolt; it is a Chu-Han duel for survival.

sentences.zh: 誼之所欲痛哭，比今為緩，抱火臥薪之喻，於今而急。

translations.literal: What Yi wished to cry bitterly for is slower compared to now; the metaphor of hugging fire and lying on kindling is urgent in the present.
translations.idiomatic: What made Jia Yi weep is graver today; we truly sleep on kindling.

sentences.zh: 大皇帝覽前代之如彼，察今勢之如此，故廣開農桑之業，積不訾之儲，恤民重役，務養戰士，是以大小感恩，各思竭命。

translations.literal: The Grand Emperor viewed former generations as thus, examined the present situation as so; therefore he broadly opened the tasks of farming and sericulture, piled stores beyond reckoning, pitied the people and weighted labor, strove to nurture fighting soldiers—therefore great and small felt gratitude, each thinking to exhaust life.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Emperor stocked grain, eased corvée, and trained troops—so every man gave his all.

sentences.zh: 斯運未至，早棄萬國，自是之後，強臣專政，上詭天時，下違從議，忘安存之本，邀一時之利，數興軍旅，傾竭府藏，兵勞民困，無時獲安。

translations.literal: This fortune had not arrived when he early cast off the myriad states; from this time strong ministers monopolized government, above deceived Heaven's seasons, below went against compliant counsel, forgot the root of safety and preservation, sought profit of one moment, repeatedly raised armies and hosts, poured out and exhausted treasury stores, troops weary and people exhausted, never obtaining peace in time.
translations.idiomatic: Since his death strongmen have misruled, wasted the treasury, and left army and people spent.

sentences.zh: 今之存者乃創夷之遺眾，哀苦之餘及耳。

translations.literal: Those who survive now are only the leftover throng of the wounded and maimed, the remainder of the pained and bitter.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors are war's cripples and grief's dregs.

sentences.zh: 遂使軍盜空匱，倉廩不實，布帛之賜，寒暑不周，重以失業，家戶不贍。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army's granaries stand empty, storehouses are not full, grants of cloth and silk do not cover cold and heat; doubled by loss of work, households cannot provide.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries are bare, stipends miss the seasons, and jobless homes cannot feed themselves.

sentences.zh: 而北積穀養民，專心向東，無復他警。

translations.literal: Yet the north piles grain and nurtures the people, whole heart turned east, no other alert.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wei piles grain and eyes only the east.

sentences.zh: 蜀為西藩，土地險固，加承先主統御之術，謂其守禦足以長久，不圖一朝奄至傾覆！

translations.literal: Shu was the western screen; its land was precipitous and solid, moreover inheriting the late lord's arts of command and control—one thought its defense could long endure; one did not reckon that in one morning it would suddenly come to overturn and collapse!
translations.idiomatic: We thought Shu a permanent shield—yet it fell overnight.

sentences.zh: 唇亡齒寒，古人所懼。

translations.literal: Lips gone, teeth cold—what the ancients feared.
translations.idiomatic: Lips gone, teeth freeze—the old warning.

sentences.zh: 交州諸郡，國之南土，交阯、九真二郡已沒，日南孤危，存亡難保，合浦以北，民皆搖動。

translations.literal: The various commanderies of Jiao Province are the state's southern soil; Jiaozhi and Jiuzhen two commanderies are already lost, Rinan stands alone and perilous, survival hard to protect; north of Hepu the people all waver.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's northern commanderies waver; the south is half lost.

sentences.zh: 因連避役，多有離叛，而備戍減少，威鎮轉輕，常恐呼吸復有變故。

translations.literal: Therefore many in linked flight from corvée have much separation and rebellion, while prepared garrison is reduced and less, awe and guard turn light; your servant always fears that in a breath again there will be sudden change.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée dodgers rebel while garrisons shrink—I fear the next breath may bring revolt.

sentences.zh: 昔海虜窺窬東縣，多得離民，地習海行，狃於往年，鈔盜無日，今胸背有嫌，首尾多難，乃國朝之厄會也。

translations.literal: In olden times sea bandits peeped at the eastern counties, got many separated people, the land practiced sea travel, grew accustomed in former years, raiding and plundering without day; now chest and back have suspicion, head and tail many difficulties—it is the state's meeting with ill fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Sea raiders once fed on our coasts; now we are vulnerable fore and aft—the state meets ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 誠宜住建立之役，先備豫之計，勉墾殖之業，為饑乏之救。

translations.literal: Truly one ought to stop the labor of building and establishing, first prepare plans of precaution, encourage the task of opening wilds, give relief to hunger and want.
translations.idiomatic: Stop palace work, prepare defense, open fields, feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 惟恐農時將過，東作向晚，有事之日，整嚴未辦。

translations.literal: Your servant fears the farming season will pass, eastern work turns late, when there is business the day, getting arrayed is not yet ready.
translations.idiomatic: I fear spring work will pass before we are ready for war.

sentences.zh: 若捨此急，盡力功作，卒有風塵不虞之變。

translations.literal: If you cast aside this urgency and exhaust strength on labor works, suddenly there is wind and dust of unforeseen change.
translations.idiomatic: Pour all strength into building and a surprise strike will find you naked.

sentences.zh: 當委版築之役，應烽燧之急，驅怨苦之眾，赴自刃之難，此乃大敵所因為資也。

translations.literal: Then you must set aside rammed-earth labor, answer beacon-fire urgency, drive a host of resentment and bitterness, go to the hardship of naked blades—this is what the great enemy relies on as capital.
translations.idiomatic: You would drop trowels for beacons and march a bitter mob with bare blades—exactly what the foe hopes for.

sentences.zh: 如但固守，曠日持久，則軍糧必乏，不待接刃，而戰士已困矣。

translations.literal: If you only firmly defend, long days and drawn-out time, then army grain will surely fail; without waiting for crossing blades the fighting soldiers are already exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Pure defense exhausts grain before a sword is crossed.

sentences.zh: 昔太戊之時，桑谷生庭，懼而修德，怪消殷興。

translations.literal: In the time of Taiwu of Yin, mulberry and grain grew in the court; he feared and cultivated virtue, prodigies vanished and Yin rose.
translations.idiomatic: King Taiwu of Yin saw mulberry and grain sprout in his hall, grew virtuous, and prospered.

sentences.zh: 熒惑守心，宋以為災，景公下從瞽史之言，而熒惑退捨，景公延年。

translations.literal: Mars guarded the heart; Song took it as disaster; Duke Jing of Song followed the blind clerk's words and Mars retreated a lodging—Duke Jing's years were extended.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Duke Jing averted Mars at the heart by heeding a blind clerk and lived longer.

sentences.zh: 夫修德於身而感異類，言發於口通神明。

translations.literal: Now to cultivate virtue in the person and move strange kinds, words issue from the mouth and penetrate spirit brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue moves prodigies; sincere words reach the gods.

sentences.zh: 臣以愚蔽，誤忝近署，不能冀宣仁澤以感靈祗，仰慚俯愧，無所投處。

translations.literal: Your servant, with foolish blindness, wrongly occupies a near office, cannot hope to spread and proclaim humane grace to move numinous powers; looking up ashamed, looking down ashamed, he has nowhere to cast himself.
translations.idiomatic: I hold a petty post yet cannot spread your grace—I am ashamed above and below.

sentences.zh: 退伏思惟，榮惑桑谷之異，天示二主，至如他余錙介之妖；

translations.literal: Retiring and lying in thought, mulberry and grain prodigies, Heaven showed the two lords; as for other trifling portents of surplus,
translations.idiomatic: I ponder how Heaven warned Yin and Song—

sentences.zh: 近是門庭小神所為，驗之天地，無有他變，而征樣符瑞前後屢臻，明珠既覿，白雀繼見，萬億之祚，實靈所挺。

translations.literal: lately are the doing of small spirits at the gate and court; checked against Heaven and earth there are no other changes, yet sign-tally auspices before and after repeatedly arrive, bright pearls already seen, white sparrows follow and appear—the fortune of a hundred million is truly what numinous potency raises.
translations.idiomatic: —while petty omens are gate-spirits; yet bright pearls and white sparrows show Heaven still favors your line.

sentences.zh: 以九域為宅，天下為家，不與編戶之民轉徙同也。

translations.literal: Taking the nine domains as house and All-under-Heaven as home is not the same as turning and migrating with registered households' people.
translations.idiomatic: The throne is not a commoner's shifting hut.

sentences.zh: 又今之宮室，先帝所營。

translations.literal: Moreover the present palace halls were built by the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: These halls were built by your father.

sentences.zh: 卜土立基，非為不祥。

translations.literal: Divining earth and setting base was not for inauspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: The site was divined—it is not ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 又楊市土地與宮連接，若大功畢竟，輿駕遷住，門行之神，皆當轉移，猶恐長，久未必勝舊。

translations.literal: Moreover Yang market's land connects with the palace; if the great work is finished to the end, imperial carriage moves to dwell, spirits of gates and roads all must shift—your servant still fears that in the long run it may not surpass the old.
translations.idiomatic: New Yang-market wings may not outshine the old halls.

sentences.zh: 屢遷不少，留則有嫌，此乃愚臣所以夙夜為憂灼也。

translations.literal: Repeated moving is not little; to stay then has blame—this is why your foolish servant from dawn to night is anxious and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Move often and court blame; stay and court blame—hence my nightly worry.

sentences.zh: 臣省《月令》，季夏之月，不可以興土功，不可以會諸侯，不可以起兵動眾，舉大事必有大殃。

translations.literal: Your servant examined the Monthly Ordinance: in the last month of summer one may not raise earthworks, may not assemble the feudal lords, may not raise troops and move the host—raising a great affair surely has great misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: The Yueling forbids summer building and mass levies—great works bring great ill.

sentences.zh: 今雖諸侯不會，諸侯之軍與會無異。

translations.literal: Now though the feudal lords do not assemble, the hosts of the feudal lords are no different from assembling.
translations.idiomatic: Your labor levies match the tabooed "host assembly."

sentences.zh: 六月戊己，土行正王，既不可犯，加又農月，時不可失。

translations.literal: Sixth month wu and ji—earth's phase is king; it already may not be violated; added to it is the farming month—season may not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Summer's earth-king phase plus harvest season must not be wasted.

sentences.zh: 昔魯隱公夏城中丘，《春秋》書之，垂為後戒。

translations.literal: In olden times Duke Yin of Lu in summer built the inner wall of Zhongqiu—the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded it, hanging as warning to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn blames Duke Yin for midsummer wall work.

sentences.zh: 今築宮為長世之洪基，而犯天地之大禁，襲《春秋》之所書，廢敬授之上務，臣以愚管，竊所未安。

translations.literal: Now building a palace as long-age great foundation yet violates Heaven and earth's great prohibition, repeats what the Spring and Autumn Annals wrote, casts aside the high task of reverently granting seasons—your servant, with foolish tube, privately finds it not secure.
translations.idiomatic: To raise a "lasting" palace now breaks heaven's summer taboo and scorns the sage's calendar—I cannot approve.

sentences.zh: 又恐所召離民，或有不至，討之則廢役興事，不討則日月滋慢。

translations.literal: Moreover your servant fears the summoned separated people may some not arrive—if you punish them then labor works are abandoned and affairs raised; if you do not punish them then days and months grow slack.
translations.idiomatic: Forced laborers may flee—punish them and work stops; ignore flight and deadlines slip.

sentences.zh: 若悉並到，大眾聚會，希無疾病。

translations.literal: If all arrive together, a great host gathers in meeting—hardly without sickness.
translations.idiomatic: Mass the people and sickness follows.

sentences.zh: 且人心安則念善，苦則怨叛。

translations.literal: Moreover when human hearts are at peace they think on good; when bitter they resent and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Ease breeds loyalty; toil breeds revolt.

sentences.zh: 江南精兵，北土所難，欲以十卒當東一人。

translations.literal: Jiangnan's picked troops are what northern soil finds hard; they wish with ten soldiers to match one eastern man.
translations.idiomatic: Ten southern veterans match one northern soldier—

sentences.zh: 天下未定，深可憂惜之。

translations.literal: All-under-Heaven is not yet settled—deeply to be worried and pitied.
translations.idiomatic: —yet the realm is unsettled; every soldier counts.

sentences.zh: 如此宮成，死叛五千，則北軍之眾更增五萬，著到萬人，則倍益十萬，病者有死亡之損，叛者傳不善之語，此乃大敵所以歡喜也。

translations.literal: If the palace is completed like this and five thousand die or rebel, then the northern host's numbers increase another fifty thousand; if ten thousand arrive, then double increase a hundred thousand; the sick have loss of death, the rebels spread words of ill—this is what the great enemy rejoices in.
translations.idiomatic: Lose five thousand builders and you swell the enemy fifty thousand; lose ten thousand and you double his host—death and desertion become his cheer.

sentences.zh: 今當角力中原，以定強弱，正於際會。

translations.literal: Now one ought to wrestle strength on the central plain to fix strong and weak, just at the border meeting.
translations.idiomatic: We must contest the Central Plain at the decisive moment.

sentences.zh: 彼益我損，加以勞困，此乃雄夫智士所以深憂。

translations.literal: They gain, we lose, added to labor and exhaustion—this is why bold men and wise knights deeply worry.
translations.idiomatic: Their gain, our loss, plus exhaustion—wise heads fear this.

sentences.zh: 臣聞先王治國無三年之儲，曰國非其國，安寧之世戒備如此。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that former kings in governing a state, without three years' store, said the state is not its state—in an age of peace and quietness guard was thus.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said no three years' grain means no state—even in peace they prepared.

sentences.zh: 況敵強大而忽農忘畜。

translations.literal: How much more the enemy strong and great while one neglects farming and forgets stores.
translations.idiomatic: How much worse when the foe is strong and you forget the plow and granary.

sentences.zh: 今雖頗種殖，間者大水沉沒，其餘存者當須耘獲。

translations.literal: Now though there has been considerable planting, recently great water drowned and sank; what survives ought still to be weeded and reaped.
translations.idiomatic: Floods have drowned the fields; what remains needs the hoe.

sentences.zh: 而長吏怖期，上方諸郡，身涉山林，盡力伐材，廢農棄務；

translations.literal: Yet the senior officials fear the deadline, upward dispatch to the various commanderies, personally wade mountains and forests, exhaust strength felling timber, abandon farming and cast aside tasks;
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates, dreading your deadline, scour the hills for timber and abandon the crop.

sentences.zh: 士民妻孥羸小，墾殖又薄；

translations.literal: gentry and commoners, wives and children, weak and small—opening wilds is moreover thin.
translations.idiomatic: Families are weak and their plots thin.

sentences.zh: 若有水旱則永無所獲。

translations.literal: If there is flood or drought then forever nothing is obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Drought or flood will then yield nothing.

sentences.zh: 州郡見米，當待有事，冗食之眾，仰官供濟。

translations.literal: Commandery and prefecture see rice—when there is to be business, the multitude who eat idly look up to official supply for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries must feed armies and idle mouths when crisis comes.

sentences.zh: 若上下空乏，運漕不供，而北敵犯疆，使周、召更生，良、平復出，不能為陛下計明矣。

translations.literal: If above and below are empty and exhausted, transport and canal do not supply, while the northern enemy violates the border, though Zhou and Shao were born again, Liang and Ping returned, they could not for Your Majesty plan—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: If stores fail when the north strikes, not even Zhou Gong could save you.

sentences.zh: 臣聞君明者臣忠，主聖者臣直，是以悽悽，昧犯天威，乞垂哀省。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that where the lord is bright the ministers are loyal, where the master is sage the ministers are straight—therefore in sorrow and fear he dimly offends Heaven's majesty, begging pity and inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The bright lord has loyal ministers—I risk your wrath to say so.

sentences.zh: 書奏，皓不納。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Hao did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao ignored the memorial.

sentences.zh: 後遷東觀令，領右國吏，核上疏辭讓。

translations.literal: Afterward he was promoted director of the Eastern Institute, concurrently right state historian; He submitted a memorial declining and yielding.
translations.idiomatic: He was later named director of the Eastern Institute and right state historian, and tried to decline.

sentences.zh: 皓答曰：“得表，以東觀儒林之府，當講校文藝，處定疑難，漢時皆名學碩儒乃任其職，乞更選英賢。

translations.literal: Hao answered saying: "I have received the memorial: the Eastern Institute is the forest of Confucian scholars; it ought to lecture and collate literary arts, settle doubtful hard points—in Han times only famed learning and great Confucians then bore that office; you beg to change selection for other outstanding worth.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao replied: "The Eastern Institute is the house of learning—you ask for another genius to collate texts as Han did.

sentences.zh: 聞之，以卿研精墳典，博覽多聞，可謂悅禮樂敦詩書者也。

translations.literal: I have heard it—because you grind fine the tomb classics and read widely and hear much, you may be called one who delights in rites and music and is earnest in the Odes and documents.
translations.idiomatic: I am told you are steeped in the classics and love ritual and poetry—

sentences.zh: 當飛翰騁藻，光贊時事，以越揚、班、張、蔡之疇，怪乃謙光，厚自菲薄，宜勉備所職，以邁先賢，勿復紛紛。”

translations.literal: You ought to fly brush and race phrases, brightly aid the affairs of the times, to surpass the class of Yang, Ban, Zhang, and Cai—strange that you are modest light and thickly belittle yourself; you ought to strive to ready what your office holds, to stride past former worthies—do not again be tangled."
translations.idiomatic: Fly your brush, outshine Yang Xiong, Ban Gu, Zhang Heng, and Cai Yong in serving the age—do not hide your lamp under a bushel; fill your post and match the ancients—no more fuss."

sentences.zh: 時倉廩無儲，世俗滋侈，核上疏曰：

translations.literal: At that time granaries had no stores, vulgar ways grew ever more extravagant; He submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Granaries stood empty while luxury spread; Hua He wrote again:

sentences.zh: 今冠虜充斥，征伐未已，居無積年之儲，出無敵之畜，此乃有國者所宣深憂也。

translations.literal: Now cap-and-diadem foes fill every quarter, campaigns and attacks do not cease; within there is no store laid by for years, without there is no hoard against the enemy—this is what those who possess a state ought deeply to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Helmets crowd the borders, war never stops, and we keep neither long-term grain nor a war chest—any ruler should tremble at that.

sentences.zh: 夫財谷所生，皆出於民，趨時務農，國之上急。

translations.literal: Now wealth and grain are born, all come from the people; hastening to the season and devoting effort to farming is the state's highest urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth and grain spring from the people; timely farming is the state's first duty.

sentences.zh: 而都下諸官，所掌別異，各自下調，不計民力，輒與近期。

translations.literal: Yet the various offices of the capital, what they administer differs each; each on its own sends down demands, not reckoning the people's strength, always setting a near deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each capital bureau issues its own quotas without regard for peasant strength or realistic deadlines.

sentences.zh: 長吏畏罪，晝夜催民，委捨佃事，遑赴會日，定送到都，或蘊積不用，而徒使百姓消力失時。

translations.literal: Senior officials fear blame, day and night urge the people, cast aside tenancy tasks, hasten to keep the meeting day, fix delivery to the capital—sometimes it piles and is not used, yet vainly makes the hundred surnames waste strength and miss the season.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates, fearing punishment, drive farmers from the fields to meet arbitrary deadlines while grain rots unused in the capital.

sentences.zh: 到秋收月，督其限入，奪其播殖之時，而責定送其今年之稅，如有逋懸，則籍沒財物，故家戶貧困，衣食不足。

translations.literal: When the month of autumn harvest comes, they supervise their limit of intake, seize the time for sowing and planting, yet require fixed delivery of this year's tax; if there is default or suspension, then they register and confiscate goods—therefore households are destitute, clothing and food insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: In harvest month they demand tax while forbidding sowing; default means confiscation—so families starve.

sentences.zh: 宜暫息眾役，專心農桑。

translations.literal: For the moment one ought to rest the multitude of labor tasks and devote heart to farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Suspend corvée and put every hand to tillage and silk.

sentences.zh: 古人稱一夫不耕，或受其饑。

translations.literal: The ancients said if one husband does not plow, perhaps someone suffers hunger.
translations.idiomatic: They said one idle husband means hunger for someone.

sentences.zh: 一女不織，或受其寒。

translations.literal: If one woman does not weave, perhaps someone suffers cold.
translations.idiomatic: One idle loom means someone goes cold.

sentences.zh: 是以先王治國，惟農是務。

translations.literal: Therefore former kings in governing states took only farming as the task.
translations.idiomatic: So the kings of old put farming first.

sentences.zh: 軍興以來，已向百栽，農人廢南畝之務，女工停機杼之業。

translations.literal: Since armies rose, already nearly a hundred years; farming men abandon the work of the southern acres, women's work stops the loom's trade.
translations.idiomatic: A century of war has idled plowmen and stilled shuttles.

sentences.zh: 推此揆之，則蔬食而長饑，薄衣而履冰者，固不少矣。

translations.literal: Pushing this and measuring it, those who eat vegetables yet long hunger, wear thin clothes yet tread on ice are certainly not few.
translations.idiomatic: Many already live on greens yet starve and wear thin cloth on ice.

sentences.zh: 臣聞主之所求於民者二，民之所望於主者三。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that what the lord seeks from the people is two, what the people hope from the lord is three.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler asks two things of the people; the people ask three of him.

sentences.zh: 二謂求其為己勞也，求其為己死也。

translations.literal: The two mean seeking that they toil for him, seeking that they die for him.
translations.idiomatic: Those two are labor and life.

sentences.zh: 三謂譏者能食之，勞者能息之，有功者能賞之。

translations.literal: The three mean that the hungry can be fed, the weary can rest, the meritorious can be rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The three are food for the hungry, rest for the weary, reward for merit.

sentences.zh: 民以致其二事而主失其三望者，則怨心生而功不建，今帑藏不實，民勞役猥，主之二求已備，民之三望未報。

translations.literal: When the people bring these two tasks yet the lord loses their three hopes, then resentment is born and achievement is not built; now treasury stores are not solid, the people labor and corvée is numerous—the lord's two seeks are already prepared, the people's three hopes are not repaid.
translations.idiomatic: You take their toil and blood yet give no food, rest, or reward—resentment rises and nothing is built.

sentences.zh: 且饑者不待美饌而後飽，寒者不俟狐貉而後溫，為味者口之奇，文繡者身之飾也。

translations.literal: Moreover the hungry do not wait for fine viands before being full; the cold do not wait for fox and badger before being warm—making flavors is the mouth's oddity, patterned embroidery is the body's ornament.
translations.idiomatic: The hungry need no banquet; the cold need no fur coat—spices and embroidery are luxuries, not needs.

sentences.zh: 今事多而役繁，民貧而俗奢，百工作無用之器，婦人為綺靡之飾，不勤麻枲，並鄉黼黻，轉相倣傚，恥獨無有。

translations.literal: Now affairs are many and corvée thick, the people are poor yet vulgar ways extravagant; the hundred crafts make useless implements, women make extravagant finery, do not work hemp and ramie, together toward embroidered insignia, turn and imitate one another, ashamed to be alone without having.
translations.idiomatic: Yet multitudes chase useless crafts and silken finery, shunning hemp until every lane apes brocade.

sentences.zh: 兵民之家，猶復遂俗，內無儋石之儲，而出有綾綺之服，至於富賈商販之家，重以金銀，奢恣尤甚。

translations.literal: In soldier and commoner households, still they follow vulgar ways; within they have not a dan or shi of store, yet without they have damask and gauze dress; as for rich merchant peddler households, doubled with gold and silver, extravagance is especially extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Even poor soldiers' wives wear silk while cupboards stay empty; merchants heap gold and outdo all in waste.

sentences.zh: 天下未平，百姓不贍，宜一生民之原，豐谷帛之業。

translations.literal: All-under-Heaven is not yet settled, the hundred surnames do not have enough; one ought to unify the root of nurturing the living, enrich the enterprise of grain and silk.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is still at war—nurture the people's root and pile up grain and cloth.

sentences.zh: 而棄功於浮華之巧，妨日於侈靡之事，上無尊卑等級之差，下有耗財物力之損。

translations.literal: Yet one casts aside achievement on flashy cleverness, wastes days on extravagant matters; above there is no difference of noble and base rank, below there is loss of wealth and material force.
translations.idiomatic: Chasing glitter wastes days and erases rank; high and low alike drain coin and strength.

sentences.zh: 今吏士之家，少無子女，多者三四，少者一二，通令戶有一女，十萬家則十萬人，人織績一歲一束，則十萬束矣。

translations.literal: Now in clerk and soldier households, few lack daughters; many have three or four, few have one or two—suppose by order each household has one daughter, a hundred thousand households then a hundred thousand people; each weaves one bolt in a year, then a hundred thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: If every household with daughters put one girl to the loom, a hundred thousand bolts a year would follow.

sentences.zh: 使四疆之內同心戮力，數年之間，布帛必積。

translations.literal: Make within the four borders hearts join in one effort; within several years cloth and silk must accumulate.
translations.idiomatic: Let the four quarters weave together and silks will fill the storehouses within a few years.

sentences.zh: 恣民五色，惟所服用，但禁綺繡無益之飾。

translations.literal: Let the people use the five colors as they will for dress, only forbid useless finery of figured silk.
translations.idiomatic: Let commoners dye what they need—only ban useless brocade.

sentences.zh: 且美貌者不待華采以祟好，艷姿者不待文綺以致愛，五采之飾，足以麗矣。

translations.literal: Moreover one of fine face does not await splendid colors to exalt beauty; one of lovely form does not await patterned silk to bring love—the ornament of five colors is enough to be lovely.
translations.idiomatic: Beauty needs no brocade; five hues of plain weave suffice for grace.

sentences.zh: 若極粉黛，窮盛服，未必無醜婦。

translations.literal: If one exhausts powder and eyebrow paint, exhausts sumptuous dress, not necessarily is there no ugly woman.
translations.idiomatic: Heaps of rouge and robes do not banish ugliness.

sentences.zh: 廢華采，去文繡，未必無美人也。

translations.literal: Cast aside splendid colors, remove patterned silk—not necessarily is there no beautiful person.
translations.idiomatic: Strip the paint and brocade—beauty does not vanish.

sentences.zh: 若實如論，有之無益廢之無損者，何愛而不斬禁以充府藏之急乎？

translations.literal: If it is truly as in the discussion—having it has no benefit, abolishing it has no harm—why love and not cut and forbid it to fill the treasury's urgency?
translations.idiomatic: If finery neither helps nor harms to lose, why not forbid it to fill urgent granaries?

sentences.zh: 此救乏之上務，富國之本業也，使管、晏復生，無以易此。

translations.literal: This is the highest task of relieving want, the root enterprise of enriching the state; were Guan and Yan born again, they could not change this.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first cure for want and the true way to enrich the state—even Guan Zhong could not improve it.

sentences.zh: 漢之文、景，承平繼統，天下已定，四方無虞，猶以雕文之妨農事，錦繡之害女紅，開富國之利，杜饑寒之本。

translations.literal: Wen and Jing of Han inherited peace in succession, All-under-Heaven was already settled, the four quarters without worry—still they took carved patterns as hindering farming, brocade embroidery as harming women's work, opened profit for enriching the state, blocked the root of hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi and Jingdi, though the realm was at peace, still banned luxuries that hurt farm and loom to stock the treasury and stop cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 況今六台分乖；

translations.literal: How much more now the six terraces split and contrary;
translations.idiomatic: How much worse now that the realm is split—

sentences.zh: 豺狼充路；

translations.literal: jackals and wolves fill the roads;
translations.idiomatic: jackals block the roads,

sentences.zh: 兵不離疆；

translations.literal: weapons do not leave the border;
translations.idiomatic: weapons never leave the frontier,

sentences.zh: 甲不解帶。

translations.literal: armor is not unbuckled.
translations.idiomatic: armor never comes off—

sentences.zh: 而可以不廣生財之原，充府藏之積哉？

translations.literal: —and can one not broaden the root of producing wealth, fill the accumulation of the treasury?
translations.idiomatic: —can you refuse to widen the sources of wealth and fill the granaries?

sentences.zh: 皓以核年老，敕令草表，核不敢。

translations.literal: Hao, because He was old in years, ordered him to draft the memorial on grass; He did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao, citing Hua He's age, ordered him to draft on straw—Hua He refused.

sentences.zh: 又敕作草文，停立待之。

translations.literal: Again he ordered him to compose a draft text, stopped and stood waiting for it.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a draft again and stood waiting.

sentences.zh: 核為文曰：

translations.literal: He composed the text saying:
translations.idiomatic: Hua He wrote:

sentences.zh: 咨核小臣，草芥凡庸。

translations.literal: Alas, petty clerk He, grass and dust, ordinary and mean.
translations.idiomatic: I, Hua He, dust and grass—

sentences.zh: 遭眷值聖，受恩特隆。

translations.literal: Meeting favor and encountering sage, receiving favor especially thick.
translations.idiomatic: —yet your favor raised me from the mire.

sentences.zh: 越從朽壤，蟬蛻朝中。

translations.literal: Crossing from rotten soil, cicada-slough in the court.
translations.idiomatic: I shed the mud like a cicada's shell and entered the purple court.

sentences.zh: 熙光紫闥；

translations.literal: Basking in light of the purple portals;
translations.idiomatic: I bask in the purple portals' light;

sentences.zh: 青璅是憑。

translations.literal: the green lock is what I lean on.
translations.idiomatic: the green door is my stay.

sentences.zh: 毖挹清露，沐浴凱風。

translations.literal: Respectfully I scoop clear dew, bathe in the triumphant wind.
translations.idiomatic: I sip clear dew and ride the royal wind.

sentences.zh: 效無絲氂，負闕山祟。

translations.literal: My effect has not a hair's tip, I bear the mountain fault of neglect.
translations.idiomatic: I have repaid no mote of your grace yet bear a mountain of fault.

sentences.zh: 滋潤含垢，恩貸累重。

translations.literal: Moistened and bearing grime, favor's loans pile heavy.
translations.idiomatic: You bore my stains and piled favor on favor.

sentences.zh: 穢質被榮，局命得融。

translations.literal: Foul substance received glory; confined fate obtained fusion.
translations.idiomatic: A worthless man gained honor and a cramped life was eased.

sentences.zh: 欲報罔極，委之皇穹。

translations.literal: Desiring to repay without limit, I entrust it to the vast azure.
translations.idiomatic: I would repay you beyond measure—only Heaven can witness.

sentences.zh: 聖恩雨注，哀棄其尤。

translations.literal: Sage favor rains down, pity casts away their worst.
translations.idiomatic: Your mercy rains down and forgives my worst faults.

sentences.zh: 猥命草對，潤被下愚。

translations.literal: Vilely ordered to draft a reply, moisture soaks the lowest fool.
translations.idiomatic: You shame me by ordering this draft to soak a fool's wit.

sentences.zh: 不敢達敕，懼速罪誅。

translations.literal: I dare not defy the order, yet fear swift crime and execution.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not refuse yet fear instant death for failure.

sentences.zh: 冒承詔命，魂逝形留。

translations.literal: Risking to receive the edict's command, soul departs while form stays.
translations.idiomatic: I obey though my soul flees and only the shell remains.

sentences.zh: 核前後陳便宜，及貢薦良能，解釋罪過，書百餘上，皆有補益，文多不悉載。

translations.literal: He before and after stated what was convenient, and presented and recommended good ability, explained and loosened guilt and faults—memorials over a hundred, all had benefit and supplement; the text is much and not fully recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a hundred memorials on policy, talent, and pardons—too many to quote.

sentences.zh: 天冊元年以微譴免，數歲卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiance he was dismissed over a slight fault; after several years he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiance a small fault cost him office; he died a few years later.

sentences.zh: 曜、核所論事章疏，咸傳於世也。

translations.literal: The memorials on affairs that Yao and He discussed were all transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao's and Hua He's papers circulated among later readers.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：薛瑩稱‘王蕃器量綽異，弘博多通。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Xue Ying said 'Wang Fan's capacity was outstanding and different, broad and learned in many connections.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ying said Wang Fan's caliber was rare and his learning wide;

sentences.zh: 樓玄清白節操，才理條暢；

translations.literal: Lou Xuan was pure and white in integrity, talent and principle orderly and smooth;
translations.idiomatic: Lou Xuan was incorrupt and lucid;

sentences.zh: 賀邵厲志高潔，機理清要。

translations.literal: He Shao set his will high and pure, his handling of topics clear and essential.
translations.idiomatic: He Shao was austere and acute;

sentences.zh: 韋曜篤學好古，博見群籍，有記述之才。

translations.literal: Wei Yao was earnest in learning and loved antiquity, saw broadly in the host of documents, had talent for recording and writing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yao loved antiquity, read everything, and could write history.

sentences.zh: ’胡沖以為‘玄、邵、蕃一時清妙，略無優劣，必不得已，玄宜在先，邵當次之。

translations.literal: ' Hu Chong thought 'Xuan, Shao, and Fan were in one stroke pure and subtle, altogether without ranking superior or inferior; if one must be forced, Xuan ought to go first, Shao next.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Chong ranked Lou Xuan first among the three pure men, He Shao second,

sentences.zh: 華核文賦之才，有過於曜，而典誥不及也。

translations.literal: Hua He's talent for rhapsody exceeded Yao's, but in edicts and directives he did not reach.
translations.idiomatic: and thought Hua He's fu surpassed Wei Yao's though his state papers did not.

sentences.zh: ’矛觀核數獻良規，期於自盡，庶幾忠臣矣。

translations.literal: ' Your servant observes that He several times presented good plans, hoping to exhaust himself—he was nearly a loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: I see Hua He as a loyal minister for his many sound plans.

sentences.zh: 然此數子，處無妄之世而有名位，強死其理，得免為幸耳。

translations.literal: Yet these several men, dwelling in an age without expectation yet possessing name and rank, violently died as reason would have it—to have escaped with their lives would have been fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in such a treacherous age fame drew a violent death—survival alone would have been luck.
